content.content:
1	---
2	title: "Export: start, then poll"
3	description: Write a file from an agent, follow the job until it finishes, stop it, and read what the file holds.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	An agent's export doesn't wait for the file. `export` checks the request, puts a job on the Export Queue and answers at once, and the agent then asks how it's going until it ends.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
13	  keys="⌘E"
14	  where="The export sheet's Add to Queue, and each row's Cancel in the Export Queue"
15	  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
16	/>
17	
18	## Write a file
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Call `export` with a preset and a path. It answers straight away.
23	
24	   ```json
25	   { "preset": "h264", "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut", "size": "1080p" }
26	   ```
27	
28	   ```json
29	   { "export_id": 3, "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut.mp4", "status": "running" }
30	   ```
31	
32	2. Call `export_status` with that `export_id`, pause, and call it again until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
33	
34	3. Read the `done` answer. It says what the file holds, including the loudness it measured and any warnings.
35	
36	</Steps>
37	
38	To stop the job, call `cancel_export`. The job shows in **Window ▸ Export Queue** like any other, but the window doesn't open by itself.
39	
40	## Export
41	
42	`export` does what **File ▸ Export…** does with **Add to Queue**, and it runs through the same writer, so an agent's file and a person's match. It takes the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)'s controls in the sheet's own terms, apart from the frame rate.
43	
44	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
45	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
46	| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding: a container and a codec. See [Presets](#presets). |
47	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, such as `~/Movies/cut.mp4`. See [Path handling](#path-handling). |
48	| `size` | string or `[width, height]` | No | The output size. See [Size](#size). |
49	| `range` | string | No | `project` for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the in and out range. See [Range](#range). |
50	| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
51	| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
52	| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalise the whole mix to this loudness, −70 to 0. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
53	| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The master limiter's ceiling, −20 to 0. See [Peak dBTP](#peak-dbtp). |
54	| `audio_bits` | integer | No | 16 or 24, for WAV and AIFF. See [Audio bits](#audio-bits). |
55	| `stems` | string | No | `tracks` or `names`, to write stems beside an audio mix. See [Stems](#stems). |
56	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draw the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything. Off by default. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
57	| `dynamic_range` | string | No | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, in an HLG project. See [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range). |
58	| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, for AV1. See [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
59	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to export, as `get_project` reports it. Without it, the frontmost project. |
60	
61	It answers `{export_id, path, status}`. `path` is the file that will be written, with `~` expanded and the extension corrected. `status` is `running` if the job started at once, or `queued` if it's waiting.
62	
63	Exports run one at a time, behind anything already in the queue. A job writes the project as it stood when `export` was called, so later edits don't reach it. Calling `export` pauses playback in that project's window.
64	
65	`export` takes no `scope`. With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open it still writes the project's timeline, not the nest's.
66	
67	## Export status
68	
69	`export_status` answers how a job is going, as its row in the Export Queue would, and it never waits. Pass the `export_id`, which is an integer of 1 or more.
70	
71	Every answer carries `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or from then to the finish once the job has ended. The rest depends on the status.
72	
73	| `status` | Also carries |
74	| --- | --- |
75	| `queued` | `waiting` while an AV1 or VP9 job is held for memory. `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
76	| `running` | `progress`, from 0 to 1. `phase` while the export names one, which is "Measuring loudness…" during the first pass over the mix. `estimated_seconds` on the same four presets. |
77	| `done` | What the file holds, in the next table. |
78	| `failed` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
79	| `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
80	
81	`estimated_seconds` is the export sheet's estimate of the whole export in whole seconds, and it's only an estimate.
82	
83	`waiting` is a sentence such as "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.1 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 7.0 GB." AV1 and VP9 exports may hold a quarter of this Mac's memory between them, though a job with no other running always starts. While one is held, a later job in the queue may run first.
84	
85	A `done` answer adds these keys.
86	
87	| Key | What it holds |
88	| --- | --- |
89	| `ok` | `true`. |
90	| `bytes` | The file's size. |
91	| `preset`, `container`, `codec` | What was written. |
92	| `width`, `height` | The file's size in pixels. These are reported on audio presets too, where they mean nothing. |
93	| `fps` | The rate as `[num, den]`, such as `[30, 1]`. |
94	| `start`, `duration` | The part of the timeline written, in [ticks](/mcp/units-and-ids/). |
95	| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the argument was on. |
96	| `dynamic_range` | The picture written: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Only for a video preset in an HLG project. |
97	| `encoder_speed` | The speed used. Only on `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
98	| `audio_bits` | The depth written. Only on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
99	| `stems` | `[{name, tracks, path}]`, one per file beside the mix. Only when `stems` was asked for. |
100	| `loudness` | What the mix measured. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
101	| `graphic_warnings` | `[{name, frame, message}]`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn, up to 64. `frame` is the graphic's own frame, or `null`. Absent when there were none. |
102	| `cursor_warnings` | `[{media, path, message}]`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn. Its clips were written without a cursor. Absent when there were none. |
103	
104	## Cancel export
105	
106	`cancel_export` stops a job, as the row's **Cancel** does, and answers as `export_status` does. Pass the `export_id`.
107	
108	| The job is | What happens |
109	| --- | --- |
110	| Queued | It's cancelled before it starts. The answer reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled before it started." |
111	| Running | It stops and its half-written file is removed. The answer may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, and `export_status` then reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled." |
112	| Finished | It's left alone, and its file stays. The answer is the finished job's. |
113	
114	## Export id and its lifetime
115	
116	An `export_id` is known until Frame Job quits. Removing a finished row from the Export Queue, or choosing **Clear Finished**, doesn't lose it, so an agent can still read how that job ended.
117	
118	An id belongs to the launch, not to a project, so `export_status` and `cancel_export` don't need `project`. Only ids that `export` answered are known. A job a person queued from the sheet has no id an agent can follow. Any other number answers "No export this launch has export_id 7 — ids come from export and last until Frame Job quits."
119	
120	## Refusals and failures
121	
122	A problem Frame Job can see from the request comes back from `export` itself as an error, and nothing is queued.
123	
124	| The request | What stops it |
125	| --- | --- |
126	| An empty timeline | "There is nothing on the timeline to export." |
127	| A folder that doesn't exist | "There is no folder at … to write into." Frame Job never creates the folder. |
128	| An unknown preset | The error lists all the presets. |
129	| An unknown `size`, or one it can't read | The error lists the sizes. See [Size](#size). |
130	| `range` of `in_out` with no range set | "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range `{start, end}`, or export with range \"project\"." |
131	| A number out of range, or a word it doesn't know | The error names the argument and the value. |
132	| An option the preset doesn't have | See [Audio bits](#audio-bits), [Stems](#stems), [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range) and [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
133	| A graphic clip in the range with no module, or a module that doesn't compile | "The export was not started: the graphic "…" does not compile — …. Fix the module and export again." It names each graphic and its first error, and it covers graphics inside nests. An audio-only preset draws no graphics, so it isn't stopped by one. |
134	
135	Anything that goes wrong after that comes back from `export_status` as `failed`, with the sentence in `reason`. Check for it even when `export` answered cleanly.
136	
137	| What went wrong | The `reason` |
138	| --- | --- |
139	| A size of another shape on a transparent preset | "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…". See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets). |
140	| A stem's file would be one of the project's media | "The stem "…" would replace media this project uses; export under another name." |
141	| A graphic fails while it's drawn | "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic "…": …. No file was written." |
142	| A retimed clip's sound, an isolated voice or a voice effect couldn't be rendered | The sentence names the clip and the reason. |
143	| A cut-out clip's masks couldn't be made | "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …." A picture cut out by **Foreground** says foreground masks. |
144	| A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser needs a loudness that hasn't been measured | "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…". Wait for the clip's analysis, then export again. |
145	| This Mac has no encoder for the preset | "This Mac cannot export with the "…" preset." |
146	
147	A failed export leaves no half-written file behind. A graphic's warnings are different: they don't stop the export, and they arrive as `graphic_warnings` in the `done` answer.
148	
149	## Presets
150	
151	There are 15 presets, one per encoding. A preset says nothing about size. These are the rows of the sheet's **Format** control, described in [Choose a format](/export/formats/). A wrong id's error lists them all.
152	
153	| Preset | In the sheet | File | Picture | Sound |
154	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
155	| `h264` | H.264 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit. What the sheet opens on. | AAC |
156	| `hevc` | HEVC (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit | AAC |
157	| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with Alpha (MOV) | `.mov` | 8-bit with transparency. Safari's transparent movie. | AAC |
158	| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC 10-bit (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
159	| `av1` | AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
160	| `av1_webm` | AV1 (WebM) | `.webm` | 10-bit | Opus |
161	| `vp9_webm` | VP9 (WebM) | `.webm` | 8-bit for an SDR picture, 10-bit for HLG and PQ. One speed. | Opus |
162	| `vp9_alpha_webm` | VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | `.webm` | Always 8-bit, with transparency. The transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play. | Opus |
163	| `prores_422` | ProRes 422 (MOV) | `.mov` | 10-bit. An editing master. | 16-bit LPCM |
164	| `prores_4444` | ProRes 4444 (MOV) | `.mov` | 12-bit with transparency. A master. | 16-bit LPCM |
165	| `audio_m4a` | Audio only (M4A) | `.m4a` | None | AAC |
166	| `audio_wav` | Audio only (WAV) | `.wav` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
167	| `audio_aiff` | Audio only (AIFF) | `.aiff` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
168	| `gif` | Animated GIF | `.gif` | 256 colours. Capped at 480 × 270. | None |
169	| `apng` | Animated PNG | `.png` | Lossless, with transparency. Capped at 960 × 540. | None |
170	
171	Macs before M3 can't play `av1` and `av1_webm` back.
172	
173	## Frame rate
174	
175	There's no frame-rate argument, so the sheet's [frame rate](/export/frame-rate/) control has no agent equivalent. An export runs at the project's rate, `gif` at 12.5 fps and `apng` at 25 fps. The `done` answer's `fps` says which, with 12.5 fps as `[25, 2]`.
176	
177	## Path handling
178	
179	The folder must exist. A `~` at the start is expanded, and an existing file at the path is replaced.
180	
181	The file always ends in the preset's extension.
182	
183	| `path` | `preset` | Writes | Why |
184	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
185	| `cut.mp4` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | The extension is already right. |
186	| `cut` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | With no extension, it's added. |
187	| `cut.mov` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | A different media extension is replaced. |
188	| `Talk v1.2` | `h264` | `Talk v1.2.mp4` | Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
189	| `cut.webm` | `h264` | `cut.webm.mp4` | `.webm` isn't one of the extensions Frame Job replaces. |
190	| `cut.mp4` | `av1_webm` | `cut.webm` | `.mp4` is. |
191	
192	The extensions it replaces are `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.m4a`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.aif`, `.aiff`, `.caf`, `.framejob`, `.srt`, `.vtt`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.heic` and `.gif`. The answer's `path` is always the file that gets written.
193	
194	## Size
195	
196	`size` is the sheet's **Size** control. See [Export size](/export/size/) for what the sizes mean to a person.
197	
198	| `size` | In the sheet | What it writes |
199	| --- | --- | --- |
200	| `document` | Document size | The project's own size. The default on every movie preset. |
201	| `2160p` | 4K | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
202	| `1440p` | 1440p | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
203	| `1080p` | 1080p | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
204	| `720p` | 720p | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
205	| `preset` | GIF default, APNG default | The format's cap. `gif` and `apng` only, where it's the default. |
206	| `[width, height]` | Custom… | Exactly this size, from 16 to 8192 pixels on each edge. |
207	
208	The number is always the short edge, and the long edge follows the project's shape, rounded to an even number. A vertical project's `1080p` is 1080 × 1920. Every size means the same on every project, so a 1920 × 1080 project's `1080p` is its own size, and a size larger than the project scales it up.
209	
210	A movie is written at exactly the size asked for. If the shape differs from the project's by more than a pixel, the picture is letterboxed. Within a pixel, it fills the frame instead.
211	
212	- **Even edges.** Every preset but `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng` needs even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. That covers `document` on a project with an odd edge. The `done` answer's `width` and `height` are the file's.
213	- **GIF and APNG.** A size is a box the picture is fitted inside, keeping its shape and never scaling up. A vertical 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default comes out at 152 × 270.
214	- **Audio presets.** A size has no effect, and `preset` isn't one of their sizes.
215	- **Transparent movies.** A `[width, height]` of another shape fails. See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets).
216	
217	An unknown size answers with the list, for example "No export size is called "480p" for h264. The sizes are: document, 2160p, 1440p, 1080p, 720p — or pass [width, height]." A custom size outside 16 to 8192 pixels is turned down the same way, not clamped.
218	
219	## Range
220	
221	`range` is the sheet's **Range** control. `project`, the default, writes the whole timeline. `in_out` writes the range set with `set_range`, and it's turned down when there's no range. See [Export a range](/export/range/).
222	
223	The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and kept inside the project. A range that comes to nothing is turned down.
224	
225	`burn_in_timecode` shows project time even in a range export, so a file written from 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 with a burn-in that reads 00:00:10:00.
226	
227	## Exact bitrates
228	
229	The sheet offers [quality](/export/quality/) tiers. An agent sets the rates directly, in bits per second, so 8 Mbps is `8000000`. Each must be a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.
230	
231	`video_bitrate` is the target video rate. Without it, the preset's own encoder settings decide. ProRes, GIF and APNG ignore it, because ProRes is fixed by its profile and the other two have no bitrate.
232	
233	On the AV1 and VP9 presets it works differently:
234	
235	- **`av1` and `av1_webm`.** It's a soft cap. The encoder works at a constant quality matched to HEVC at that rate, and the file usually comes in well under it. Very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over. Without it, the quality is matched to HEVC at 0.07 bits per pixel per frame.
236	- **`vp9_webm`.** It's a soft cap too, matched to HEVC, or HEVC 10-bit in an HDR export. Up to about 1.15 times over was measured.
237	- **`vp9_alpha_webm`.** It's the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone. The transparency's stream comes on top, at about 6–15 % of the video at 1080p, and up to about 39 % at 640 × 360, as measured.
238	
239	`audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate, 192 kbps when absent. Opus takes the nearest rate its encoder offers. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it, because they write LPCM.
240	
241	## The loudness report
242	
243	Every export with sound measures its own mix and reports it as `loudness` in the `done` answer, normalised or not. GIF and APNG have no sound, and a timeline with no sound has nothing to measure, so `loudness` is absent from both.
244	
245	`loudness_lufs` normalises the whole mix to an integrated loudness, from −70 to 0. The sheet's [Loudness](/export/loudness/) rows are −14 for streaming, −16 for podcasts and −23 for EBU R 128 broadcast, and an agent can ask for any value, such as −14.5. The export measures itself first, then applies one gain to everything, through the master limiter. The file lands on the target with its loudest peaks limited, rather than the whole mix held down. GIF and APNG ignore it.
246	
247	| Key | What it holds |
248	| --- | --- |
249	| `summary` | The same line the queue row and the progress sheet show, such as "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −16.0 LUFS", with " · peaks limited by 8.6 dB" when the limiter took 0.05 dB or more. |
250	| `integrated_lufs` | The file's integrated loudness. Absent when it has none, and `summary` then says "loudness not measurable". |
251	| `true_peak_dbtp` | The file's true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
252	| `sample_peak_dbfs` | The file's sample peak, never above the true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
253	| `gain_db` | The gain applied to reach the target. |
254	| `ceiling_dbtp` | The master limiter's ceiling. |
255	| `limited_db` | How far the limiter turned the loudest peak down. |
256	| `capped_by_gain` | `true` when the +40 dB limit on the gain decided it, so the file may be short of the target. |
257	| `target_lufs` | The `loudness_lufs` asked for. Absent when none was. |
258	
259	A programme shorter than one 400 ms measuring block, or one too quiet to pass the standard's gate, has a peak and no integrated loudness. Digital silence reads "Silent" in `summary`.
260	
261	## Peak dBTP
262	
263	Every export with sound goes through a master limiter, so the file's true peak stays at or under a ceiling. `peak_dbtp` sets that ceiling, from −20 to 0. It's −1 when absent, which is the sheet's fixed value. 0 is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off.
264	
265	You can pass it with or without `loudness_lufs`. `limited_db` in the [report](#the-loudness-report) says how far the limiter turned the loudest peak down.
266	
267	## Audio bits
268	
269	`audio_bits` is the sheet's [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/) control: 16, the default, or 24. It's rounded once from the mix and never dithered, and the `done` answer repeats it.
270	
271	It works on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other preset the answer is "h264 has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset. ProRes keeps 16-bit sound. Any other number is turned down whatever the preset.
272	
273	## Stems
274	
275	`stems` also writes [stems](/export/stems/) beside the mix, on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. It's the sheet's **Stems** control.
276	
277	| `stems` | What it writes |
278	| --- | --- |
279	| `tracks` | One file per heard track. |
280	| `names` | One file per track name. Heard tracks whose names match, ignoring case, share a file, and an unnamed track gets its own. |
281	
282	A track is heard when it has sound in it and isn't muted or silenced by another track's solo. Each stem is named `<file> - <track name>.<ext>`, beside the mix, so `mix.wav` and a track called Voice give `mix - Voice.wav`. An unnamed track is `Track N`, `/` and `:` in a name become `-`, and two stems that would share a name are told apart with ` (Track N)`.
283	
284	A stem holds its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness gain and no limiter, so the stems add up to the mix wherever the master changed nothing. Any file already at a stem's name is replaced.
285	
286	The `done` answer lists each one as `stems [{name, tracks, path}]`. `tracks` holds the ids of the timeline tracks in that stem.
287	
288	- On any other preset the answer is "h264 has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset.
289	- With no track heard, it's "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write".
290	- If a stem's file would be one of the project's media, the job fails before any stem is written, and `export_status` gives the reason.
291	- A failed or cancelled job leaves neither the mix nor any stem behind.
292	
293	## Dynamic range
294	
295	`dynamic_range` chooses the picture an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/) writes. It's the sheet's **Dynamic Range** control.
296	
297	| `dynamic_range` | What it writes |
298	| --- | --- |
299	| `hlg` | BT.2100 HLG, with no Dolby Vision. The default on the presets that carry HDR. |
300	| `pq` | HDR10: BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², with a P3-D65 mastering display of 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0. |
301	| `sdr` | The project's SDR version. |
302	
303	The presets that carry HDR are `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`. Every other video preset in an HLG project writes the SDR version, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, and audio presets ignore the argument.
304	
305	- `hlg` or `pq` on another video preset answers "h264 is 8-bit and writes the SDR version; export dynamic_range "pq" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444".
306	- `hlg` or `pq` in an SDR project answers "dynamic_range "pq" needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first".
307	- `sdr` in an SDR project changes nothing.
308	
309	Once a job is `done`, `dynamic_range` in the answer names the picture that was written. An SDR project's answer has no such key.
310	
311	## Encoder speed
312	
313	`encoder_speed` trades export time for file size on `av1` and `av1_webm`. It's the sheet's [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) control, and the `done` answer names the one used.
314	
315	| `encoder_speed` | SVT-AV1 preset | What it does |
316	| --- | --- | --- |
317	| `faster` | 8 | The quickest. |
318	| `balanced` | 6 | The default. |
319	| `smaller` | 4 | The smallest file for the picture, and the slowest. |
320	
321	On every other preset the answer is "h264 has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm", naming the preset. That includes `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`, which have one speed.
322	
323	## Transparent presets
324	
325	Four presets keep a transparent canvas transparent: `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`, `vp9_alpha_webm` and `apng`. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). A GIF can show a fully transparent pixel, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partial survives.
326	
327	On the three movie presets, a `[width, height]` of a different shape from the canvas can't be written, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. `export` queues the job, and `export_status` then reads `failed` with a reason that names both sizes. The shape is judged after an odd edge is evened, and within a pixel the picture fills the frame, so a size in the canvas's own proportions always works, at any scale. Every named size already has the canvas's shape.
328	
329	`apng` fits its picture inside the size instead, so this doesn't apply to it.
330

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

213	            throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
214	        }
215	        let ids = rows.map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
216	        if let id = raw as? String {
217	            guard let row = rows.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
218	                throw ToolError(
219	                    message: "No export size is called \"\(id)\" for \(preset). The sizes "
220	                        + "are: \(ids) — or pass [width, height].")
221	            }
222	            return (row.width, row.height)
223	        }
224	        if let array = raw as? [Any], array.count == 2 {
225	            let edges = array.compactMap(Self.wholeEdge)
226	            if edges.count == 2 {
227	                let range = ExportSheetController.sizeRange
228	                // Each refusal of a `size` offers the OTHER spelling: the
229	                // unknown-id one above names the custom form, and this one
230	                // names the rows, so a caller who meant a standard size and
231	                // reached for numbers has the ids in front of it.
232	                guard edges.allSatisfy(range.contains) else {
233	                    throw ToolError(
234	                        message: "A custom size must be \(range.lowerBound)…\(range.upperBound) "
235	                            + "px on each edge, not [\(edges[0]), \(edges[1])] — or pass a "
236	                            + "row: \(ids).")
237	                }
238	                return (edges[0], edges[1])
239	            }
240	        }
241	        throw ToolError(
242	            message: "size must be a row of the export sheet's Size popup — \(ids) — or "
243	                + "[width, height] in px, not \(Self.spelled(raw)).")
244	    }
245	
246	    /// One edge of a custom size as a whole number, or nil for a value that
247	    /// is not one — which sends the whole `size` to the refusal that names
248	    /// it. The coercion `intArg` applies holds: a string spelling of a whole
249	    /// number is a JSON-typing slip, not a different request. A fraction is
250	    /// refused rather than truncated, since 1920.5 is not a width the caller
251	    /// can have meant. So is a boolean: JSON's `true` arrives as an
252	    /// `NSNumber` like any other and would read as 1 through it, and the
253	    /// Core Foundation type is the one thing that still tells `true` from
254	    /// `1`.
255	    private static func wholeEdge(_ value: Any) -> Int? {
256	        if let number = value as? NSNumber {
257	            guard CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID() else { return nil }
258	            let real = number.doubleValue
259	            return real.isFinite && real == real.rounded() ? number.intValue : nil
260	        }
261	        return (value as? String).flatMap(Int.init)
262	    }
263	
264	    /// A refusal from `rc_export_settings` or `rc_export_sizes` as the tool's
265	    /// error. The core's message passes through as it was, with one
266	    /// addition: an unknown preset id — the message that begins
267	    /// "unknown export preset", the same words from either call
268	    /// (`export.rs`) — gets the ids the table does take appended, because
269	    /// without them it is the one error a model cannot correct itself from,
270	    /// since nothing else lists the table. A refused bitrate or range keeps
271	    /// its own message alone: a list of presets under it would be a false
272	    /// lead.
273	    private static func coreRefusal(_ error: any Error) -> ToolError {
274	        let message = error.localizedDescription
275	        guard message.hasPrefix("unknown export preset") else {
276	            return ToolError(message: message)
277	        }
278	        let names = ReelExport.presets().map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
279	        return ToolError(message: "\(message). The presets are: \(names).")
280	    }
281	
282	    /// A caller's value as it was spelled, for a refusal that names it: its
283	    /// JSON where it is JSON, its Swift description otherwise.
284	    private static func spelled(_ raw: Any) -> String {
285	        guard JSONSerialization.isValidJSONObject([raw]),
286	            let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(
287	                withJSONObject: raw, options: [.fragmentsAllowed]),
288	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
289	        else { return String(describing: raw) }
290	        return text
291	    }

295	/// What a finished export's answer carries: the resolved settings and the
296	/// facts about the file that was written, read off the queue's job once it
297	/// has finished — `export_status`'s `done` answer

299	/// `export` itself answered before it returned at once.

302	    /// The `done` answer's keys, exactly the ones `export` answered when it
303	    /// blocked to the file. `bytes` is the file's size as read at the finish.
304	    static func exportResult(
305	        settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, path: String, bytes: Int,
306	        loudness: ExportLoudness?, graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning],
307	        cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
308	    ) -> [String: Any] {
309	        var result: [String: Any] = [
310	            "ok": true,
311	            "path": path,
312	            "bytes": bytes,
313	            "preset": settings.preset,
314	            "container": settings.container,
315	            "codec": settings.codec,
316	            "width": settings.width,
317	            "height": settings.height,
318	            "fps": [settings.fps.num, settings.fps.den],
319	            "start": settings.start,
320	            "duration": settings.duration,
321	            // Not one of the resolved settings — the core never saw it — but
322	            // it is a fact about the file that was written, and every other
323	            // key here is one too.
324	            //
325	            // What it establishes is exactly one link and not the chain: this
326	            // is `options.burnInTimecode`, the local decoded a few lines up,
327	            // so a caller reading it back knows the argument was READ rather
328	            // than dropped in argument reading — the failure `boolArg`'s
329	            // refusal covers from the other side. It does NOT say the writer
330	            // used it; only a pixel can say that, and
331	            // `tools/proof/phase7_proof.py` is where one does.
332	            "burn_in_timecode": burnInTimecode,
333	        ]
334	        // The picture an HLG project's file was written as (`hlg`, `pq` or
335	        // `sdr`); absent for every SDR project and audio row.
336	        if let color = settings.color {
337	            result["dynamic_range"] = color
338	        }
339	        // The speed the `av1` row was encoded at (spec §11 CX-12 (2)); absent elsewhere.
340	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed {
341	            result["encoder_speed"] = speed.rawValue
342	        }
343	        // The depth a WAV or AIFF was written at (spec §11 AU-29); absent elsewhere.
344	        if let bits = settings.audioBits {
345	            result["audio_bits"] = bits
346	        }
347	        // Each stem written beside the mix, in order (spec §11 AU-108); absent without.
348	        if !settings.stems.isEmpty {
349	            let mix = URL(fileURLWithPath: path)
350	            result["stems"] = settings.stems.map {
351	                [
352	                    "name": $0.name, "tracks": $0.tracks,
353	                    "path": ExportStemsPipeline.url(for: $0, mix: mix).path,
354	                ] as [String: Any]
355	            }
356	        }
357	        if let measured = loudnessResult(loudness) {
358	            result["loudness"] = measured
359	        }
360	        if let warned = graphicWarningsResult(graphicWarnings) {
361	            result["graphic_warnings"] = warned
362	        }
363	        if let warned = cursorWarningsResult(cursorWarnings) {
364	            result["cursor_warnings"] = warned
365	        }

369	    /// What the export's sound MEASURED, for the result — nil, and then the
370	    /// key is simply absent, wherever `Exporter` published no report: a
371	    /// format that holds no audio track at all (GIF and APNG), and a
372	    /// timeline with no sound in it, which is the case a caller actually
373	    /// meets. A missing `loudness` is therefore "there was nothing to
374	    /// measure", never "the measurement was skipped".
375	    ///
376	    /// This is `detect_silence`'s posture applied to the writer: the numbers
377	    /// are read back off the file's own mix rather than repeated from the
378	    /// request, so a caller can check that a −14 LUFS export actually landed
379	    /// at −14, which is what makes phase 5's ±0.5 LU claim a claim anyone can
380	    /// test over MCP. `target` is what was ASKED for and is absent when
381	    /// nothing was — every export measures itself and reports, normalised or
382	    /// not.
383	    ///
384	    /// It is read off the queue's job (`ExportQueueController.Job.loudness`),
385	    /// which `finished` copies from the `Exporter` before dropping it:
386	    /// `Exporter.finish` publishes the report before it calls back, so every
387	    /// consumer (this, the queue's row and the progress sheet) reads it after
388	    /// the completion has fired.
389	    ///
390	    /// Every level goes through `jsonLevel`: a silent programme measures
391	    /// −∞ dBTP, and `JSONSerialization` throws on an infinity — which would
392	    /// report a successful export as a failed tool call.
393	    static func loudnessResult(_ report: ExportLoudness?) -> [String: Any]? {
394	        guard let report = report else { return nil }
395	        var measured: [String: Any] = [
396	            // The same sentence the progress sheet's last line shows, so the
397	            // two consumers of one measurement cannot describe it differently.
398	            "summary": report.summary,
399	            "true_peak_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.truePeakDBTP),
400	            // The shifted sample peak, never above the true peak the master
401	            // held (spec §11 AU-28).
402	            "sample_peak_dbfs": jsonLevel(
403	                min(report.measured.samplePeakDBFS + report.gainDB, report.truePeakDBTP)),
404	            "gain_db": report.gainDB,
405	            "ceiling_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.ceiling),
406	            "limited_db": report.limitedDB,
407	            "capped_by_gain": report.cappedByGain,
408	        ]
409	        // Absent rather than null, and for a reason worth the line: a
410	        // programme shorter than one 400 ms gating block, or one whose every
411	        // block fell under the standard's absolute gate, HAS no integrated
412	        // loudness. `summary` says so in words.
413	        if let integrated = report.integratedLUFS, integrated.isFinite {
414	            measured["integrated_lufs"] = integrated
415	        }
416	        if let target = report.target {
417	            measured["target_lufs"] = target
418	        }
419	        return measured
420	    }

422	    /// Each distinct warning the export's graphics gave while the file was
423	    /// drawn (G-24 (c)), `[{name, frame, message}]` — `frame` the graphic's
424	    /// own, null when it has none — or nil, and then the key is absent,
425	    /// when there was none. Read off the queue's job after the completion,
426	    /// as `loudnessResult` is: `Exporter.finish` publishes it before the
427	    /// unpin. A failed export answers as it did.
428	    static func graphicWarningsResult(_ warnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]) -> [[String: Any]]? {
429	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return nil }
430	        return warnings.map {
431	            ["name": $0.name, "frame": $0.frame ?? NSNull(), "message": $0.message] as [String: Any]
432	        }

437	    /// absent, when there was none — `graphicWarningsResult`'s shape (G-24 (c)).
438	    static func cursorWarningsResult(_ warnings: [ExportCursorWarning]) -> [[String: Any]]? {
439	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return nil }
440	        return warnings.map {
441	            ["media": $0.media, "path": $0.path, "message": $0.message] as [String: Any]
442	        }
443	    }

449	/// The agent's half of the Export Queue (spec §11 #326): `export` enqueues a
450	/// job in `ExportQueueController.shared` and answers its id at once, and the
451	/// two tools here follow it. `export_status` mirrors Window ▸ Export Queue's
452	/// row for that job (`ExportQueueWindowController`) — its state, its progress
453	/// bar, its phase and its closing sentence — and `cancel_export` mirrors the
454	/// row's Cancel button, which calls the same `ExportQueueController.cancel`.
455	///
456	/// **Only ids `export` returned are reachable.** A person's own queued job has
457	/// no record here and is answered as unknown: the mirror follows what the
458	/// agent started, not the queue as a whole.
459	///
460	/// **A record outlives its row.** The queue drops a finished job on Remove or
461	/// Clear Finished, and an agent that asks after that must still hear how it
462	/// ended, so `AgentExports` copies each tracked job's state on every queue
463	/// change — synchronously, on main, inside the queue's own post — and stamps
464	/// the finish (its time and the file's size) on its first terminal sight.
465	/// Records last for the launch and hold no project handle or graphic set.
466	extension AgentServer {
467	
468	    /// `export_status {export_id}` — the row of Window ▸ Export Queue for a job
469	    /// `export` started, read now; it never waits.
470	    func exportStatus(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
471	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
472	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
473	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
474	        }
475	        return try jsonResult(status)
476	    }
477	
478	    /// `cancel_export {export_id}` — the Export Queue row's Cancel. A queued
479	    /// or running job is cancelled through the queue (a running one answers
480	    /// through the writer, so it may still read `running` here); a finished
481	    /// one is left alone and answered as it is.
482	    func cancelExport(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
483	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
484	        guard AgentExports.shared.status(id) != nil else {
485	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
486	        }
487	        if let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id), !job.state.isFinished {
488	            ExportQueueController.shared.cancel(id)
489	        }
490	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
491	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
492	        }
493	        return try jsonResult(status)
494	    }

496	    /// The word a status answer spells a queue state with.
497	    static func exportStatusWord(_ state: ExportQueueController.State) -> String {
498	        switch state {
499	        case .waiting: return "queued"
500	        case .running: return "running"
501	        case .completed: return "done"
502	        case .failed: return "failed"
503	        case .cancelled: return "cancelled"
504	        }

529	/// last seen, plus what the `done` answer needs that the job does not carry.
530	private struct AgentExportRecord {
531	    let settings: ExportSettings
532	    let burnInTimecode: Bool
533	    /// `systemUptime` at the `export` handler's first line.
534	    let started: TimeInterval
535	    var state: ExportQueueController.State
536	    var progress: Double
537	    var phase: String?
538	    var message: String?
539	    var destination: URL
540	    var loudness: ExportLoudness?
541	    var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]
542	    /// The media whose cursor file was not drawn (spec §11 CU-37 (c)).
543	    var cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
544	    /// `systemUptime` at the first terminal sight, nil until then.
545	    var finished: TimeInterval?
546	    /// The file's size as read at that finish.
547	    var bytes: Int = 0
548	
549	    mutating func copy(_ job: ExportQueueController.Job) {
550	        state = job.state
551	        progress = job.progress
552	        phase = job.phase
553	        message = job.message
554	        destination = job.destination
555	        loudness = job.loudness
556	        graphicWarnings = job.graphicWarnings
557	        cursorWarnings = job.cursorWarnings
558	        guard job.state.isFinished, finished == nil else { return }
559	        finished = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
560	        bytes =
561	            (try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: job.destination.path)[.size])
562	            .flatMap { ($0 as? NSNumber)?.intValue } ?? 0
563	    }
564	}

566	/// The records of every export the agent started this launch, by the queue's
567	/// job id. Main thread only, like the queue it reads.
568	final class AgentExports {
569	    static let shared = AgentExports()
570	
571	    private var records: [UInt64: AgentExportRecord] = [:]
572	    private var observer: NSObjectProtocol?
573	
574	    private init() {
575	        // `queue: nil` runs the block synchronously inside the queue's own
576	        // post, so a terminal state is copied before any Remove can drop it.
577	        observer = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
578	            forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification,
579	            object: ExportQueueController.shared, queue: nil
580	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.refresh() }
581	    }
582	
583	    /// Starts following a job `export` just enqueued. Reads it AT ONCE: an
584	    /// early refusal finishes inside `enqueue`, before this is called, so its
585	    /// terminal post has already gone by.
586	    func track(
587	        _ id: UInt64, settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, started: TimeInterval
588	    ) {
589	        // Never nil: `enqueue` appends the job before it returns, an early
590	        // refusal only finishes it in place, and the only removals (`remove`,
591	        // `clearFinished`) are the queue window's button actions, which cannot
592	        // run inside the one main-thread block that enqueues and calls this.
593	        guard let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id) else { return }
594	        var record = AgentExportRecord(
595	            settings: settings, burnInTimecode: burnInTimecode, started: started,
596	            state: job.state, progress: job.progress, phase: job.phase, message: job.message,
597	            destination: job.destination, loudness: job.loudness,
598	            graphicWarnings: job.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: job.cursorWarnings)
599	        record.copy(job)
600	        records[id] = record
601	    }
602	
603	    /// The `export_status` answer for `id`, or nil for an id `export` never
604	    /// returned this launch.
605	    func status(_ id: UInt64) -> [String: Any]? {
606	        guard let record = records[id] else { return nil }
607	        let end = record.finished ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
608	        var answer: [String: Any] = [:]
609	        switch record.state {
610	        case .running:
611	            answer["progress"] = record.progress
612	            if let phase = record.phase { answer["phase"] = phase }
613	        case .completed:
614	            answer = AgentServer.exportResult(
615	                settings: record.settings, burnInTimecode: record.burnInTimecode,
616	                path: record.destination.path, bytes: record.bytes, loudness: record.loudness,
617	                graphicWarnings: record.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: record.cursorWarnings)
618	        case .failed, .cancelled:
619	            answer["reason"] = record.message ?? ""
620	        case .waiting:
621	            // The memory hold's sentence, present only while held (spec §11 CX-18).
622	            if let held = record.message { answer["waiting"] = held }
623	        }
624	        if record.state == .waiting || record.state == .running,
625	            let seconds = ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: record.settings)
626	        {
627	            answer["estimated_seconds"] = Int(seconds.rounded())
628	        }
629	        answer["export_id"] = id
630	        answer["status"] = AgentServer.exportStatusWord(record.state)
631	        answer["path"] = record.destination.path
632	        answer["elapsed"] = ((end - record.started) * 1000).rounded() / 1000
633	        return answer
634	    }
635	
636	    /// Copies every unfinished tracked job from the queue.
637	    private func refresh() {
638	        let queue = ExportQueueController.shared
639	        for (id, record) in records where record.finished == nil {
640	            guard let job = queue.job(id) else { continue }
641	            var updated = record
642	            updated.copy(job)
643	            records[id] = updated
644	        }
645	    }
646	}

10	//! Export presets and the resolution of one into concrete settings
11	//! (spec §7.8).
12	//!
13	//! Rust decides, AVFoundation does: nothing here encodes anything. The job
14	//! is to turn "H.264, 1920 × 1080, the in/out range, 30 fps" into the exact
15	//! set of values Swift hands to the writer — the preset name, the output
16	//! file type, the time range, the frame size — so that the choice of format
17	//! is testable without a GPU and the MCP agent's `export` tool takes the
18	//! same vocabulary the UI does.
19	//!
20	//! A preset is an ENCODING — a container and a codec — and carries no size:
21	//! an export is at the document's own size unless one is asked for, and
22	//! the sizes on offer for a document and a format are a separate list,
23	//! [`Project::export_sizes`] in `export_size.rs`, whose rows reach the
24	//! resolver here as the same `width`/`height` overrides a script sends.
25	//!
26	//! Two of the presets name a format AVFoundation cannot write at all: an
27	//! animated GIF and an animated PNG are assembled frame by frame through
28	//! ImageIO. That changes nothing here except one field — those rows carry
29	//! no `avf_preset`, and a null `avf_preset` is Swift's signal to take the
30	//! image-sequence path instead of building a session. Everything else
31	//! (the size, the rate, the range, the file's UTI) is resolved identically,
32	//! because it means the same thing on either path.
33	//!
34	//! Four rows, `av1` (spec §11 CX-12), `av1_webm` (CX-15), `vp9_webm`
35	//! (CX-16) and `vp9_alpha_webm` (CX-17), are encoded by a bundled library
36	//! and not by AVFoundation, which still writes `av1`'s container (the core
37	//! writes the three WebMs): their `writer` names the route, and on the two
38	//! AV1 rows `encoder_speed` names SVT-AV1's speed; no other row's settings
39	//! carry either key, and the two VP9 rows' carry no speed, libvpx having one
40	//! (CX-3).
41	//!
42	//! The two uncompressed audio rows, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`, carry
43	//! `audio_bits`, 16 or 24 (spec §11 AU-29): 16 when not asked, and refused
44	//! by name on every other row.
45	//!
46	//! The three audio rows take `stems`, `tracks` or `names` (spec §11
47	//! AU-108): asked, the settings end with `stems`, the files beside the mix
48	//! resolved to `[{name, tracks}]` by `export_stems.rs`; a movie row refuses.
49	//!
50	//! The preset table is the single source of truth: [`presets`] serializes
51	//! it for the picker and [`Project::export_settings`] resolves against the
52	//! same rows, so a preset cannot exist in the menu and not in the resolver.
53	//!
54	//! How an override value is READ and REFUSED is `export_overrides.rs`,
55	//! and the rows themselves — the containers, and the presets written into
56	//! them — are `export_table.rs`. The vocabulary and the table: this file
57	//! is the design they serve and the resolution that brings the two of
58	//! them together against one project.
