89	impl Project {
90	    /// Resolves `preset_id` plus optional `overrides` against this project
91	    /// into the concrete settings Swift configures the export session with
92	    /// (`rc_export_settings`).
93	    ///
94	    /// Overrides may set `width`, `height`, `fps` (`[num, den]`), `range`
95	    /// (`{"start", "duration"}` in ticks), `optimize_for_network`, the two
96	    /// bitrates `video_bitrate` / `audio_bitrate` (bits per second,
97	    /// strictly positive), the two loudness figures `loudness_lufs` /
98	    /// `peak_dbtp`, `dynamic_range` (`hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, spec §11
99	    /// HD-14), `encoder_speed` (`faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, on a
100	    /// row whose bundled encoder has speeds, CX-12, CX-16) and `audio_bits`
101	    /// (16 or 24, on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`, AU-29) and `stems`
102	    /// (`tracks` or `names`, on the three audio rows, resolved to
103	    /// `[{name, tracks}]` last in the settings, AU-108); anything else in the object is ignored, so a newer UI
104	    /// can send fields this build does not know. Each is read and refused
105	    /// by `export_overrides.rs`, which is where the spelling of every one
106	    /// of them lives.
107	    ///
108	    /// A bitrate is emitted only when it was asked for. There is no default
109	    /// to fall back on (see `export_table::PRESETS`), and an absent key says
110	    /// exactly that — "let the encoder pick" — where a zero or a null would
111	    /// have to be re-interpreted as the same thing on the Swift side. The two
112	    /// are accepted for every preset, including the ones that cannot use them,
113	    /// on the same principle that reports a width for the audio-only row:
114	    /// one rule for reading overrides, and the format flags say what the
115	    /// output can actually carry.
116	    ///
117	    /// The two loudness figures follow the bitrates exactly — emitted only
118	    /// when asked for, accepted by every preset, either one alone: the
119	    /// ceiling is the export's master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27), which runs
120	    /// with or without a target.
121	    ///
122	    /// The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and clamped to the
123	    /// project, because an `AVAssetExportSession` `timeRange` that begins
124	    /// between two frames starts the export on a frame the user did not
125	    /// choose. A range that resolves to zero length is refused: an empty
126	    /// export is always a mistake, and AVFoundation reports it far later
127	    /// and far less clearly.
128	    ///
129	    /// `Err` for an unknown preset or a malformed override. This is a QUERY
130	    /// and not an edit: there is no "changes nothing" case, so it has no
131	    /// identity arm and no refusal arm (spec §5.5).
132	    pub fn export_settings(
133	        &self,
134	        preset_id: &str,
135	        overrides: Option<&Value>,
136	    ) -> Result<Value, String> {
137	        let preset = preset(preset_id)?;
138	        let overrides = object(overrides)?;
139	        // The picture the row writes (spec §11 HD-14 (c), `dynamic_range.rs`):
140	        // read before anything else, so a mistyped value is refused by name
141	        // whatever the row, and resolved against the canvas and the row.
142	        let picture = self.deliverable(preset, dynamic_range(overrides)?)?;
143	        // The bundled encoder's speed (spec §11 CX-12 (2)): read on any row
144	        // so a misspelling is named, then refused on a row it cannot apply
145	        // to, and Balanced when a writer row was not asked.
146	        let speed = match (encoder_speed(overrides)?, preset.takes_encoder_speed()) {
147	            (Some(_), false) => {
148	                return Err(format!(
149	                    "{} has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm",
150	                    preset.id
151	                ))
152	            }
153	            (asked, true) => Some(asked.unwrap_or(EncoderSpeed::Balanced)),
154	            (None, false) => None,
155	        };
156	        // The uncompressed rows' bit depth (spec §11 AU-29), on the speed's
157	        // terms: read on any row so a 20 is named, refused on a row that
158	        // has no depth to choose, and 16 on those rows when not asked.
159	        let bits = match (audio_bits_override(overrides)?, preset.takes_audio_bits()) {
160	            (Some(_), false) => {
161	                return Err(format!(
162	                    "{} has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff",
163	                    preset.id
164	                ))
165	            }
166	            (asked, true) => Some(asked.unwrap_or(16)),
167	            (None, false) => None,
168	        };
169	        // The stems (spec §11 AU-108 (a)), on the depth's terms: read on any
170	        // row so a misspelling is named, refused on a movie row, and
171	        // resolved to the files they are only when asked.
172	        let stems = match (stems_override(overrides)?, preset.takes_stems()) {
173	            (Some(_), false) => {
174	                return Err(format!(
175	                    "{} has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff",
176	                    preset.id
177	                ))
178	            }
179	            (Some(mode), true) => Some(self.export_stems(mode)?),
180	            (None, _) => None,
181	        };
182	
183	        // Size: the preset's cap if it has one, else the canvas — a movie
184	        // preset renders at whatever the project composites at, and a size
185	        // the sheet's popup or a script chose arrives as the override.
186	        let (preset_width, preset_height) = preset
187	            .size
188	            .unwrap_or((self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height));
189	        let width = positive_u32(overrides, "width")?.unwrap_or(preset_width);
190	        let height = positive_u32(overrides, "height")?.unwrap_or(preset_height);
191	        // What is reported is the size the FILE will have, so that the
192	        // sheet's readout, its Size popup and the `export` tool's result
193	        // all say the numbers the writer draws (`export_size.rs` has both
194	        // rules and their reasons). An image format is written with the
195	        // picture FITTED inside the size, never letterboxed and never
196	        // upscaled, so its numbers are the fit and not the box. A row that
197	        // needs even dimensions writes an odd edge one pixel smaller
198	        // (spec §11 G-33), whether the edge came from the canvas or was
199	        // asked for. Every other row writes the pair as it stands.
200	        let (width, height) = if preset.fits_inside_size() {
201	            crate::export_size::fit_within((self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height), (width, height))
202	        } else if preset.even_sized() {
203	            crate::export_size::even_size((width, height))
204	        } else {
205	            (width, height)
206	        };
207	
208	        // The preset's rate, else the canvas — the image-sequence presets
209	        // cap the rate for the same reason they cap the size, and every
210	        // movie preset exports at the rate the project was cut at.
211	        let fps = fps_override(overrides, preset.fps.unwrap_or(self.canvas.fps))?;
212	
213	        let project_duration = self.duration();
214	        let (mut start, mut duration) = range_override(overrides, (0, project_duration))?;
215	        // Snap first, then clamp: snapping can only move a bound by less
216	        // than a frame, so clamping afterwards cannot be undone by it.
217	        start = time::snap_to_frame(start, fps).clamp(0, project_duration);
218	        duration =
219	            time::snap_to_frame(duration, fps).clamp(0, project_duration.saturating_sub(start));
220	        if duration <= 0 {
221	            return Err(format!(
222	                "export range is empty: {duration} ticks at {start} in a project {project_duration} ticks long"
223	            ));
224	        }
225	
226	        // Bits per second, or nothing at all. No preset supplies one, so an
227	        // absent key here reaches Swift as an absent key there and means
228	        // "the encoder's own ladder".
229	        let video_bitrate = positive_u32(overrides, "video_bitrate")?;
230	        let audio_bitrate = positive_u32(overrides, "audio_bitrate")?;
231	
232	        // The integrated loudness target and the master limiter's true-peak
233	        // ceiling, on the bitrates' terms: emitted only when asked for, so
234	        // an absent `loudness_lufs` reaches Swift as an absent key and means
235	        // "do not normalise", and an absent `peak_dbtp` the master's default
236	        // (spec §11 AU-27). The reader is the one place their bounds live.
237	        let (loudness_lufs, peak_dbtp) = loudness(overrides)?;
238	
239	        let optimize = boolean(
240	            overrides,
241	            "optimize_for_network",
242	            preset.container.optimizes_for_network(),
243	        )?;
244	
245	        let mut range = Map::new();
246	        range.insert("start".to_string(), Value::from(start));
247	        range.insert("duration".to_string(), Value::from(duration));
248	
249	        let mut out = Map::new();
250	        out.insert("preset".to_string(), Value::from(preset.id));
251	        // Null here means "AVFoundation cannot write this" — the GIF and
252	        // APNG rows — and is Swift's cue to take the ImageIO path. It is
253	        // NOT "pick a session preset yourself".
254	        out.insert(
255	            "avf_preset".to_string(),
256	            match preset.avf_preset {
257	                Some(name) => Value::from(name),
258	                None => Value::Null,
259	            },
260	        );
261	        out.insert(
262	            "container".to_string(),
263	            Value::from(preset.container.as_str()),
264	        );
265	        out.insert(
266	            "file_type".to_string(),
267	            Value::from(preset.container.file_type()),
268	        );
269	        out.insert("codec".to_string(), Value::from(preset.codec));
270	        // Width and height are reported even for the audio-only preset —
271	        // they cost nothing and let the sheet show one summary line for
272	        // every preset — but `video: false` is what Swift keys off.
273	        out.insert("width".to_string(), Value::from(width));
274	        out.insert("height".to_string(), Value::from(height));
275	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(Some(fps)));
276	        if let Some(bps) = video_bitrate {
277	            out.insert("video_bitrate".to_string(), Value::from(bps));
278	        }
279	        if let Some(bps) = audio_bitrate {
280	            out.insert("audio_bitrate".to_string(), Value::from(bps));
281	        }
282	        if let Some(lufs) = loudness_lufs {
283	            out.insert("loudness_lufs".to_string(), Value::from(lufs));
284	        }
285	        if let Some(dbtp) = peak_dbtp {
286	            out.insert("peak_dbtp".to_string(), Value::from(dbtp));
287	        }
288	        out.insert("range".to_string(), Value::Object(range));
289	        // Audio is offered whenever the container can hold it: a project
290	        // with no sound simply produces no audio track, which is cheaper
291	        // than deciding here. A GIF or an APNG holds none at all.
292	        out.insert(
293	            "audio".to_string(),
294	            Value::from(preset.container.carries_audio()),
295	        );
296	        out.insert("video".to_string(), Value::from(preset.video));
297	        // Whether the ENCODING carries a fourth channel — true for
298	        // `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` and `apng`, and for nothing else the
299	        // table offers. `export_table.rs`'s `alpha` field doc is where
300	        // `apng` against `gif` is argued — a GIF shows a transparent pixel
301	        // and still answers false, because it has one palette index and no
302	        // fourth channel — and `core/tests/export.rs` pins the three rows
303	        // by name.
304	        //
305	        // It reads `preset.alpha` and not `self.canvas.background`, which
306	        // is the whole decision and is worth one sentence here as well as
307	        // in the field doc: this object is flat and one shape for every
308	        // row, so a flag that answered "the canvas is translucent" would
309	        // say `alpha: true` on an H.264, a GIF and a WAV — three files with
310	        // nowhere to put it. It is `audio`'s kind of fact, one line up, and
311	        // told the same way: what the file can HOLD, never what this
312	        // document happens to be. A transparent canvas written through a
313	        // row that answers FALSE composites onto black, and this is the key
314	        // that lets the sheet and the `export` tool say so before the file
315	        // exists.
316	        out.insert("alpha".to_string(), Value::from(preset.alpha));
317	        out.insert("optimize_for_network".to_string(), Value::from(optimize));
318	        // An HLG project's video row names the picture it writes (spec §11
319	        // HD-14 (c)): `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`; only then, so every SDR project's
320	        // settings are the text they were and an audio row is unchanged.
321	        if let Some(picture) = picture {
322	            out.insert("color".to_string(), Value::from(picture.as_str()));
323	        }
324	        // The encoder route on a writer row, and its speed where the encoder
325	        // has speeds, so every other row's settings are the text they were
326	        // (spec §11 CX-12, CX-16 (1)).
327	        if let Some(writer) = preset.writer {
328	            out.insert("writer".to_string(), Value::from(writer.as_str()));
329	        }
330	        if let Some(speed) = speed {
331	            out.insert("encoder_speed".to_string(), Value::from(speed.as_str()));
332	        }
333	        // The depth on the two uncompressed rows only, so every other row's
334	        // settings are the text they were (spec §11 AU-29).
335	        if let Some(bits) = bits {
336	            out.insert("audio_bits".to_string(), Value::from(bits));
337	        }
338	        // The stems last, and only when asked, so every other export's
339	        // settings are the text they were (spec §11 AU-108).
340	        if let Some(stems) = stems {
341	            let stems = stems.iter().map(|stem| stem.to_json()).collect();
342	            out.insert("stems".to_string(), Value::Array(stems));
343	        }
344	        Ok(Value::Object(out))
345	    }
346	}
347	//! One row of the export table (spec §7.8): [`Preset`], what each row
348	//! answers about itself, and [`fps_json`], the rate's one spelling.
349	//!
350	//! Moved whole out of `export_table.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md:
351	//! a module at ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on),
352	//! as codec-export C5's toll T1, a pure move. `export_table.rs` re-exports
353	//! both, so every `crate::export_table::Preset` and
354	//! `crate::export_table::fps_json` path holds; `name` and `to_json` became
355	//! `pub(crate)` because the table's rows and `presets` stay behind.
356	
357	use serde_json::{Map, Value};
358	
359	use crate::export_container::Container;
360	use crate::export_encoder::{EncoderSpeed, Writer};
361	use crate::time::Fps;
362	
363	/// One row of the table. Crate-visible so `export_size.rs` can read the
364	/// cap and the codec of the row it lists sizes for, and so `export.rs`'s
365	/// resolver can read the rest, both through [`preset`]; every field is
366	/// `pub(crate)` because the table's rows are built in `export_table.rs`.
367	pub(crate) struct Preset {
368	    pub(crate) id: &'static str,
369	    pub(crate) name: &'static str,
370	    pub(crate) container: Container,
371	    pub(crate) codec: &'static str,
372	    /// False for the three audio-only presets; every other row carries
373	    /// video.
374	    pub(crate) video: bool,
375	    /// Whether this ENCODING carries an alpha channel — `hevc_alpha`,
376	    /// `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_4444` and `apng`, and nothing else. It says what the FILE can
377	    /// hold, and never that a particular canvas is translucent:
378	    /// `export_settings`
379	    /// emits one flat object for every row, so a flag derived from the
380	    /// project's background would report `alpha: true` on an H.264, a GIF
381	    /// and a WAV, which reads as a defect from either side of the FFI. A
382	    /// transparent canvas exported through a row with no fourth channel
383	    /// simply composites onto black, and the flag is what lets the sheet
384	    /// and the `export` tool say so before the file exists.
385	    ///
386	    /// **It is a `Preset` field and not a [`Container`] question**, which
387	    /// is the one thing worth arguing here, because the neighbouring
388	    /// capability [`Container::carries_audio`] IS a container question and
389	    /// the two look alike. Whether a file can hold a sound track is decided
390	    /// by the container's format — a GIF has no audio track to put samples
391	    /// in whatever you encode — so it is answered once for the container.
392	    /// A fourth channel is decided by the CODEC: `Container::Mov` hosts
393	    /// `prores_422` and `prores_4444` alike, and 422 cannot carry alpha at
394	    /// any bitrate, so a container-level answer would have to be wrong for
395	    /// one of the two rows. Same shape of fact, different owner.
396	    ///
397	    /// **`gif` is false and `apng` is true, and the difference is the word
398	    /// CHANNEL.** Both can show a transparent pixel, so both look alike
399	    /// from the outside and a reader who has exported one will call this
400	    /// row a mistake. APNG is true colour with a real fourth channel and a
401	    /// pixel may be any fraction of opaque. A GIF has ONE palette index
402	    /// nominated as transparent: a pixel is either that index or fully
403	    /// opaque, there is no partial value to store, and a soft edge against
404	    /// nothing comes out as a hard jagged one. A flag that answered "yes"
405	    /// for both would license the sheet to promise a translucent GIF.
406	    /// Measured on the way in, not assumed: an `apng` export of a
407	    /// transparent canvas decodes `pix_fmt=rgba` with its corner at
408	    /// alpha 0, and a `gif` of the same timeline decodes with the corner
409	    /// transparent through its palette and no partial value anywhere.
410	    pub(crate) alpha: bool,
411	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas size", which is what every movie
412	    /// row wants: a preset is an encoding, and the size is the document's
413	    /// unless a `width`/`height` override says otherwise. The resolver
414	    /// fills the canvas in for the audio-only rows too, so every settings
415	    /// object carries a width. Only the two image rows pin one — the cap
416	    /// `Project::export_sizes` lists as their default.
417	    pub(crate) size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
418	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas rate", which is what every movie
419	    /// preset wants. Only the image-sequence rows pin one, because their
420	    /// cost is frames × pixels and nothing else.
421	    pub(crate) fps: Option<Fps>,
422	    /// The `AVAssetExportSession` preset name, verbatim; `None` for a
423	    /// container AVFoundation cannot write.
424	    ///
425	    /// Since phase 5 the field means only **"AVFoundation can write this
426	    /// row"**, and the name itself is a record rather than an instruction.
427	    /// Nothing has run a session since M2, but `null` here is still the
428	    /// one thing routing an export to the ImageIO writer
429	    /// (`ExportSettings.isImageSequence` is literally `avPreset == nil`),
430	    /// so a row that AVFoundation writes must carry SOME name even when
431	    /// AVFoundation has no name for it. There is no `AVAssetExportPreset`
432	    /// for LPCM in a WAV or an AIFF, so those two rows carry the audio-only
433	    /// name `audio_m4a` carries: it is the closest true statement
434	    /// available — "an audio-only file AVFoundation writes" — and a null
435	    /// there would hand a WAV to `ImageSequenceWriter`, which would refuse
436	    /// it as an unknown image container and report a format this table
437	    /// advertises as unsupported. A name also means "the composition is
438	    /// read back through AVFoundation" (spec §11 CX-15), which is all it says
439	    /// on `av1_webm` and `vp9_webm`, whose files the core writes.
440	    pub(crate) avf_preset: Option<&'static str>,
441	    /// The bundled encoder that writes the row's video, or `None` for
442	    /// AVFoundation's own encoders (ImageIO where `avf_preset` is null).
443	    /// A row with a writer takes `encoder_speed` when its encoder has
444	    /// speeds (`Writer::takes_speed`).
445	    pub(crate) writer: Option<Writer>,
446	}
447	
448	/// A rate as the two-element `[num, den]` array the spec spells every rate
449	/// with, or null for "the project's own". One function so the preset row
450	/// and the resolved settings cannot disagree about the shape.
451	pub(crate) fn fps_json(fps: Option<Fps>) -> Value {
452	    match fps {
453	        Some(fps) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(fps.num), Value::from(fps.den)]),
454	        None => Value::Null,
455	    }
456	}
457	
458	impl Preset {
459	    /// True for the rows written frame by frame through ImageIO — the ones
460	    /// with no session preset — whose picture is FITTED inside the size
461	    /// rather than letterboxed to it, so a size on them is a box and the
462	    /// resolved numbers are the fit (`export_size::fit_within`).
463	    pub(crate) fn fits_inside_size(&self) -> bool {
464	        self.video && self.avf_preset.is_none()
465	    }
466	
467	    /// True for the rows whose frame has to have EVEN pixel dimensions:
468	    /// every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444 (spec §11 G-33). On
469	    /// these an odd edge is resolved one pixel smaller, in the size list's
470	    /// Document row and in the resolved settings alike
471	    /// (`export_size::even_size`), so the size reported is the size the
472	    /// writer writes.
473	    ///
474	    /// It is asked of `avf_preset` and the codec rather than listed row by
475	    /// row, so a new AVFoundation row is even-sized until someone exempts
476	    /// it — the safe side, since 4:2:0 chroma needs it and a row that can
477	    /// keep an odd edge has to be measured doing so, as ProRes 4444 was
478	    /// (`ExporterWriter+Settings.swift`'s `encodedSize`). The audio-only
479	    /// rows answer true: they have no picture and go on reporting what
480	    /// `h264` reports. The two image rows answer false; their numbers are
481	    /// the fit (`fits_inside_size`), odd or not.
482	    pub(crate) fn even_sized(&self) -> bool {
483	        self.avf_preset.is_some() && self.codec != "prores4444"
484	    }
485	
486	    /// True for a row whose bundled encoder has speeds, the rows
487	    /// `encoder_speed` applies to (spec §11 CX-12 (2), CX-16 (2)).
488	    pub(crate) fn takes_encoder_speed(&self) -> bool {
489	        self.writer.is_some_and(Writer::takes_speed)
490	    }
491	
492	    /// True for the uncompressed audio rows, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`,
493	    /// the rows `audio_bits` applies to (spec §11 AU-29). ProRes's LPCM
494	    /// track keeps 16 bits; it is not an `lpcm` row.
495	    pub(crate) fn takes_audio_bits(&self) -> bool {
496	        self.codec == "lpcm"
497	    }
498	
499	    /// True for the three audio-only rows, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and
500	    /// `audio_aiff`, the rows `stems` applies to (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
501	    pub(crate) fn takes_stems(&self) -> bool {
502	        !self.video
503	    }
504	
505	    pub(crate) fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
506	        let mut out = Map::new();
507	        out.insert("id".to_string(), Value::from(self.id));
508	        out.insert("name".to_string(), Value::from(self.name));
509	        out.insert(
510	            "container".to_string(),
511	            Value::from(self.container.as_str()),
512	        );
513	        out.insert("codec".to_string(), Value::from(self.codec));
514	        out.insert("video".to_string(), Value::from(self.video));
515	        out.insert(
516	            "size".to_string(),
517	            match self.size {
518	                Some((w, h)) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(w), Value::from(h)]),
519	                None => Value::Null,
520	            },
521	        );
522	        // `size` and `fps` are spelled the same way for the same reason:
523	        // null is "whatever the project is" — the document size, the
524	        // document rate — which the resolver fills in from the canvas.
525	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(self.fps));
526	        out.insert(
527	            "avf_preset".to_string(),
528	            match self.avf_preset {
529	                Some(name) => Value::from(name),
530	                None => Value::Null,
531	            },
532	        );
533	        if crate::dynamic_range::HDR_ROWS.contains(&self.id) {
534	            out.insert("hdr".to_string(), Value::from(true));
535	        }
536	        if let Some(writer) = self.writer {
537	            out.insert("writer".to_string(), Value::from(writer.as_str()));
538	            if writer.takes_speed() {
539	                let speeds = EncoderSpeed::ALL.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str()));
540	                out.insert("encoder_speeds".to_string(), speeds.collect());
541	            }
542	        }
543	        if self.takes_audio_bits() {
544	            let bits = [16, 24].iter().map(|b| Value::from(*b));
545	            out.insert("audio_bits".to_string(), bits.collect());
546	        }
547	        if self.takes_stems() {
548	            let modes = ["tracks", "names"].iter().map(|m| Value::from(*m));
549	            out.insert("stems".to_string(), modes.collect());
550	        }
551	        Value::Object(out)
552	    }
553	}
554	//! The export table: the closed set of files Frame Job can write, and
555	//! nothing whatever about writing one of them (spec §7.8).
556	//!
557	//! Split out of `export.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md: a module
558	//! at ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on), which
559	//! that file paid once already — `describe` and the override readers went
560	//! to `export_overrides.rs` in road map 2's phase 5, and this is the
561	//! second cut, taken in phase 7 for the same reason and along a different
562	//! seam. The rule both follow: cut where somebody can NAME the line, and
563	//! re-export the piece taken out whole, so not one path anywhere else
564	//! changes.
565	//!
566	//! # The seam: a fact about the world, not about a document
567	//!
568	//! Everything in this file is a constant, and none of it can be
569	//! influenced by a project. [`Container`] is the set of files this
570	//! application knows how to produce and the four questions each one
571	//! answers about ITSELF — its extension, its UTI, whether a leading index
572	//! is worth rewriting, whether it can hold sound at all. [`Preset`] is one
573	//! encoding placed in one of those containers, and [`PRESETS`] is every
574	//! such row in menu order. An APNG's type identifier is PNG's whatever
575	//! the timeline holds; GIF caps its size because of what a palettised
576	//! frame-by-frame format costs, not because of anybody's canvas.
577	//!
578	//! `export.rs` keeps the other half, and the other half is the one with a
579	//! `&self`: `Project::export_settings` is the only code that reads a
580	//! canvas, a duration, a rate or an override, and it is where those meet
581	//! a row from here. So the line runs between them in one direction only —
582	//! the resolver knows the table, the table knows nothing about a project
583	//! — which is also why the module doc that explains the whole export
584	//! design stays over there rather than following the rows here. This file
585	//! says what CAN be written. That one says what this particular document,
586	//! written that way, comes out as.
587	//!
588	//! # Paths
589	//!
590	//! `export.rs` re-exports [`presets`] and [`preset`] at their old names,
591	//! so `crate::export::presets()` (`ffi_query.rs`) and
592	//! `crate::export::preset(id)` (`export_size.rs`) resolve exactly as they
593	//! did — the same trick, and for the same reason, as the `describe`
594	//! re-export sitting a few lines above them. What the cut did cost is
595	//! visibility, mechanically: the [`Preset`] fields the resolver reads and
596	//! the four [`Container`] questions it asks are `pub(crate)` now, where
597	//! one file had been able to keep them private. [`fps_json`] came across
598	//! with the table rather than staying with the resolver and is
599	//! `pub(crate)` for it: both sides spell a rate, and its being one
600	//! function is the whole of why they cannot disagree about the shape.
601	
602	use serde_json::Value;
603	
604	pub(crate) use crate::export_container::Container;
605	pub(crate) use crate::export_encoder::{EncoderSpeed, Writer};
606	pub(crate) use crate::export_preset::{fps_json, Preset};
607	use crate::time::Fps;
608	
609	/// The §7.8 set: one row per ENCODING, in menu order. A row is a container
610	/// and a codec and nothing else — no size, no rate — so an export is at the
611	/// document's own size and rate unless a person asks for another, through
612	/// the Size popup the sheet fills from `Project::export_sizes` or the
613	/// overrides a script sends. The size used to be part of the row ("H.264
614	/// 1080p", "HEVC 4K"), and that shape made the format menu two questions
615	/// asked as one: picking HEVC meant picking 1080p or 4K with it, and a
616	/// 1440p or a vertical document had no row that fit it at all. Two
617	/// questions get two controls, and the format is only ever the encoding.
618	///
619	/// The two image rows are the exception and keep a size and a rate,
620	/// because for them the numbers ARE what makes the row worth having: a GIF
621	/// or an APNG costs frames × pixels with no inter-frame prediction to
622	/// spend against, so "at the document's size and rate" is a file no one
623	/// can send, and the cap is the point of the format rather than a default
624	/// it happens to carry (§7.8; the row comments argue each number). Both
625	/// caps are still defaults a size or fps override replaces, and
626	/// `export_sizes` lists each as the first row of its list.
627	///
628	/// The FIRST row is the default: `rc_export_presets` is "in menu order"
629	/// and the export sheet opens on its first entry, so whatever sits here is
630	/// what ⌘E writes unless a person picks otherwise. H.264 in MP4 is the
631	/// file every player and every upload form takes, which is why it leads
632	/// and HEVC — half the size, not yet everywhere — follows.
633	///
634	/// Each movie row carries an `AVAssetExportSession` preset name for the
635	/// record: the three "highest quality" names are the ones a session would
636	/// take the composition's own size under rather than fit it to a fixed
637	/// frame, which is exactly a row with no size of its own. Nothing runs a
638	/// session any more (§7.8), so on the Swift side the name is only the
639	/// signal that AVFoundation can write the row at all; the two image rows
640	/// carry none, which is the signal to write them frame by frame through
641	/// ImageIO instead. The two LPCM rows repeat `audio_m4a`'s name for the
642	/// same reason and with the field doc's caveat: AVFoundation has no
643	/// session preset for LPCM, and a null would route a WAV to ImageIO.
644	///
645	/// **No row carries a default bitrate, deliberately.** On the session path
646	/// the preset name IS the ladder — `AVAssetExportSession` exposes no way to
647	/// set a rate — so a number here would be one the export cannot honour,
648	/// which is worse than none at all. On the writer path VideoToolbox derives
649	/// a rate from the frame size, which beats any constant this table could
650	/// hold: one that suits 4K wastes half the file at 720p. ProRes is fixed by
651	/// its profile and ignores a request outright, and GIF and APNG have no
652	/// bitrate to set. A bitrate is therefore something the user asks for — the
653	/// `video_bitrate` / `audio_bitrate` overrides — never something a preset
654	/// assumes on their behalf.
655	const PRESETS: [Preset; 15] = [
656	    // The default (see above). The ids are the `export` tool's vocabulary
657	    // and every script that calls it spells them, so a row is named for
658	    // the encoding alone — `h264`, not `h264_document` — because the size
659	    // is no longer anything the id could say.
660	    Preset {
661	        id: "h264",
662	        name: "H.264 (MP4)",
663	        container: Container::Mp4,
664	        codec: "h264",
665	        video: true,
666	        alpha: false,
667	        size: None,
668	        fps: None,
669	        avf_preset: Some("AVAssetExportPresetHighestQuality"),
670	        writer: None,
671	    },
672	    Preset {
673	        id: "hevc",
674	        name: "HEVC (MP4)",
675	        container: Container::Mp4,
676	        codec: "hevc",
677	        video: true,
678	        alpha: false,
679	        size: None,
680	        fps: None,
681	        avf_preset: Some("AVAssetExportPresetHEVCHighestQuality"),
682	        writer: None,
683	    },
684	    // HEVC with an alpha channel (spec §11 G-33), directly after the row it
685	    // is a variant of. It is the DELIVERY row that keeps transparency — a
686	    // title or a lower third a web page or another editor plays over its
687	    // own background, at HEVC's size where `prores_4444` is a master — and
688	    // it is a MOV because that is the container AVFoundation writes the

980	//! The output sizes the export sheet offers for one document and one
981	//! format — `rc_export_sizes` (spec §7.8) — and the one rule for what a
982	//! size MEANS on an image format, which `export_settings` applies too.
983	//!
984	//! A preset is an encoding and carries no size (`export.rs`), so the size
985	//! is a second choice, and this module is the list that choice is made
986	//! from: the format's cap if it has one, the document's own size, and the
987	//! standard sizes fitted to the document's aspect. The FIRST row is the
988	//! default — the rule every list the export sheet is built from follows —
989	//! which is the document's size for a movie format and the cap for an
990	//! image format, because an image format's cap is the point of the row
991	//! and not a ceiling that only applies from above.
992	//!
993	//! **The number is the short edge.** A standard size is named by one
994	//! number, and the number people use is the short one: "1080p ultrawide"
995	//! is 2560 × 1080 and "1080p vertical" is 1080 × 1920, and both are 1080p
996	//! to everyone who says it. Naming by the long edge would call the
997	//! ultrawide 2560p and the vertical 1920p, which nobody does. So a row
998	//! keeps its short edge exactly and the long edge follows the document:
999	//! L = S × long / short of the document, on whichever axis the document is
1000	//! longer along, and S × S for a square.
1001	//!
1002	//! **The long edge is rounded to even.** 4:2:0 chroma puts one colour
1003	//! sample under each 2 × 2 block of luma, so H.264 and HEVC want even
1004	//! dimensions, and `ExporterWriter.evenDimension` rounds an odd one down
1005	//! before writing. Rounding here — to the nearest even integer, a tie
1006	//! going up — means the size the popup shows is the size the file has;
1007	//! leaving it to the writer would change the size behind the sheet's
1008	//! back.
1009	//!
1010	//! **The even rule (spec §11 G-33).** The same is true of the document row
1011	//! and of any size asked for, so on every row that needs even dimensions
1012	//! (`Preset::even_sized`: every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444)
1013	//! the size is resolved HERE, by [`even_size`]: the document row's numbers
1014	//! in this list, and in `export_settings` whatever was asked. An odd edge
1015	//! is one pixel SMALLER. Down, because that is the size the writer already
1016	//! wrote, so the report moves to the file and no file changes size;
1017	//! because rounding up would hand the encoder a frame larger than the
1018	//! picture on that axis; and because every listed row is then its own
1019	//! fixed point, as an image format's is. The row is named "Document
1020	//! (even)" when its numbers are not the canvas's, which is the whole of
1021	//! how the popup says why. The argument this replaces was that a "Document
1022	//! size" that was not the document's size would be a lie; the lie was the
1023	//! row that said 321 × 181 over a file of 320 × 180. ProRes 4444 and the
1024	//! two image formats keep an odd edge, and their row is "Document size",
1025	//! the canvas as it is.
1026	//!
1027	//! **An image format's numbers are the file's.** A GIF or an APNG is
1028	//! written frame by frame with the picture FITTED inside the size — aspect
1029	//! kept, never upscaled — where a movie is letterboxed to exactly the frame
1030	//! asked for (`ExporterImageSequence`, spec §7.8): padding costs bytes in
1031	//! every frame for pixels that carry nothing, and a bigger frame carries no
1032	//! more detail. So on those two formats every row here, and every size
1033	//! `export_settings` resolves — the cap, a standard row, a custom size — is
1034	//! the canvas fitted inside that box ([`fit_within`]), so that the popup,
1035	//! the sheet's readout and the `export` tool all report the numbers the
1036	//! file will have: a vertical 1080 × 1920 timeline's "GIF default" is
1037	//! 152 × 270, not 480 × 270. The fit is decided here, once; the writer
1038	//! draws each frame at exactly this size and does not fit a second time.
1039	//! It is also its own fixed point — a fitted size fed back as the box
1040	//! fits to itself — because that is exactly what happens: the sheet and
1041	//! the tool send a listed row's numbers back through `export_settings` as
1042	//! `width` and `height`, and a fit that could move a derived edge by a
1043	//! pixel on the second pass would show one size and write another.
1044	//!
1045	//! **Rows may repeat.** A 1920 × 1080 document's 1080p row IS the document
1046	//! row, and on a 1080 × 1920 document every image-format row from 1080p up
1047	//! is the document again. They are listed anyway, because an id is the
1048	//! `export` tool's vocabulary and a request for `1080p` has to mean the
1049	//! same thing on every document — refusing it exactly where it is a no-op
1050	//! would be the popup's tidiness leaking into an API. The sheet hides a
1051	//! row whose numbers an earlier row already has, so a person never sees one
1052	//! size under two names, and the row that shows is the one whose name says
1053	//! more ("Document size" over "1080p"). Rows larger than the document are
1054	//! offered for a movie — they were before, as the 4K preset — because a
1055	//! 720p screen recording exported at 4K for a platform that picks its
1056	//! bitrate by resolution is a real request.
1057

1065	/// only for 4K, which nobody calls 2160p out loud but which needs a
1066	/// short-edge id to sit in the same vocabulary as the other three.
1067	const STANDARD: [(&str, &str, u32); 4] = [
1068	    ("2160p", "4K", 2160),
1069	    ("1440p", "1440p", 1440),
1070	    ("1080p", "1080p", 1080),

1077	    name: String,
1078	    width: u32,

1085	        out.insert("id".to_string(), Value::from(self.id));

1087	        out.insert("width".to_string(), Value::from(self.width));
1088	        out.insert("height".to_string(), Value::from(self.height));

1096	    /// `rc_export_sizes` returns, in menu order — the first is the default.
1097	    ///
1098	    /// The rows:
1099	    ///
1100	    /// 1. `preset` — the format's cap, "GIF default" / "APNG default", for
1101	    ///    the two rows of the table that carry one; nothing for the rest.
1102	    /// 2. `document` — "Document size", the canvas as it is; on a row that
1103	    ///    needs even dimensions the canvas evened ([`even_size`]), named
1104	    ///    "Document (even)" when that is not the canvas's own size.
1105	    /// 3. `2160p` ("4K"), `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p` — the short edge named,
1106	    ///    the long edge fitted to the canvas and rounded to even.
1107	    ///
1108	    /// On an image format every row's numbers are the canvas fitted inside
1109	    /// that row's box, never upscaled — the size the file will have. Rows
1110	    /// may repeat an earlier row's numbers and are listed anyway (the
1111	    /// module doc says why); the sheet hides the repeats.
1112	    ///
1113	    /// One list for every movie format, the audio-only row included: a
1114	    /// width is reported for it the way `export_settings` reports one, and
1115	    /// the sheet disables the control rather than this module keeping a
1116	    /// second rule for one row. `Err` for an unknown preset, naming it —
1117	    /// the same lookup and the same words as `export_settings`.
1118	    pub fn export_sizes(&self, preset_id: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
1119	        let preset = export::preset(preset_id)?;
1120	        let document = (self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height);
1121	        let fits = preset.fits_inside_size();
1122	        let sized = |(width, height): (u32, u32)| {
1123	            if fits {
1124	                fit_within(document, (width, height))
1125	            } else {
1126	                (width, height)
1127	            }
1128	        };
1129	
1130	        let mut rows: Vec<Row> = Vec::new();
1131	        if let Some(cap) = preset.size {
1132	            // The codec in capitals is the format's name as people write
1133	            // it — GIF, APNG — for the two rows that carry a cap.
1134	            let (width, height) = sized(cap);
1135	            rows.push(Row {
1136	                id: "preset",
1137	                name: format!("{} default", preset.codec.to_uppercase()),
1138	                width,
1139	                height,
1140	            });
1141	        }
1142	        // The id is `document` either way: the name is the popup's, and it
1143	        // changes only when the numbers are not the canvas's.
1144	        let listed = if preset.even_sized() {
1145	            even_size(document)
1146	        } else {
1147	            document
1148	        };
1149	        let name = if listed == document {
1150	            "Document size"
1151	        } else {
1152	            "Document (even)"
1153	        };
1154	        rows.push(Row {
1155	            id: "document",
1156	            name: name.to_string(),
1157	            width: listed.0,
1158	            height: listed.1,
1159	        });
1160	        for (id, name, short) in STANDARD {
1161	            let (width, height) = sized(fitted(document, short));
1162	            rows.push(Row {
1163	                id,
1164	                name: name.to_string(),
1165	                width,
1166	                height,
1167	            });
1168	        }
1169	
1170	        Ok(Value::Array(rows.iter().map(Row::to_json).collect()))
1171	    }

1175	/// `height` document: the long edge is `short` × the document's long edge
1176	/// over its short one, rounded to the nearest even integer with a tie
1177	/// going up, on the axis the document is longer along. A square document
1178	/// gives `short` × `short`.

1194	    let long = u32::try_from(half * 2).unwrap_or(u32::MAX - 1);

1215	/// A `width` × `height` canvas fitted inside a box: the canvas itself when
1216	/// it already fits — never upscaled — and otherwise scaled down, aspect
1217	/// kept, so that the edge which meets the box first takes the box's value
1218	/// exactly and the other is the scaled value rounded UP to a whole pixel.
1219	/// The rule an image format's size means (module doc), shared by
1220	/// `export_settings` and [`Project::export_sizes`] so the two cannot
1221	/// disagree about what a GIF will measure.
1222	///
1223	/// Up rather than to the nearest, so that the fit is its own fixed point.
1224	/// Fitting the result again compares box × canvas products on the two
1225	/// axes, and the derived edge — never below its exact value — keeps the
1226	/// same axis limiting, whose derived edge is the same ceiling; rounded to
1227	/// the nearest it can fall below the exact value, flip the limiting axis
1228	/// on the second pass, and take a pixel off the other edge (a 3024 × 1964
1229	/// recording's 1080p box, 1662 × 1080, came back 1662 × 1079 and then
1230	/// 1661 × 1079). The ceiling never leaves the box: the limiting axis is
1231	/// the one whose exact scaled value fits, and a whole number no smaller
1232	/// than a value that fits inside a whole box edge fits too.
1233	pub(crate) fn fit_within((width, height): (u32, u32), (box_w, box_h): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
1234	    if width <= box_w && height <= box_h {
1235	        return (width, height);
1236	    }
1237	    let (w, h) = (u64::from(width).max(1), u64::from(height).max(1));
1238	    let (bw, bh) = (u64::from(box_w).max(1), u64::from(box_h).max(1));
1239	    // The width meets the box first when box_w / w ≤ box_h / h, which is
1240	    // box_w × h ≤ box_h × w with no division to round.
1241	    let (fw, fh) = if bw * h <= bh * w {
1242	        (bw, ceil_div(h * bw, w))
1243	    } else {
1244	        (ceil_div(w * bh, h), bh)
1245	    };
1246	    let edge = |value: u64| u32::try_from(value).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).max(1);
1247	    (edge(fw), edge(fh))
1248	}

1250	/// `a / b` rounded up to a whole number; `b ≥ 1`.
1251	fn ceil_div(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 {
1252	    a.div_ceil(b)

//! An HLG project's deliverables (spec §11 HD-5, HD-14): which picture an
//! export row writes — the HLG master, HDR10 (PQ) or the SDR version — and the
//! two refusals that keep a file from carrying a picture it cannot label.
//!
//! The vocabulary is three words, `hlg`, `pq` and `sdr`, spelled
//! `dynamic_range` both as an export override (`export_overrides.rs` reads it)
//! and as a recipe option (`recipe_options.rs`), because the two are one
//! decision seen from two sides: the export publishes its settings' `color` as
//! the recipe option of the key it draws, so the output pass the preview draws
//! for Show SDR Version is the one the file is written through.
//!
//! An SDR project is untouched by all of it: `deliverable` answers `None` for
//! every row there, so its settings carry no `color` and its recipes no
//! `dynamic_range`, and every SDR file and frame is the text and the bytes it
//! was.

use crate::export_table::Preset;

568	/// The app-wide account of the bundled-encoder exports running now (spec §11 CX-18): the
569	/// Export Queue's job and every Export… progress sheet's, each booked from just before its
570	/// exporter starts to its finish, at the resident peak `ExportEncoderCosts.memory` measured
571	/// for its key and size.
572	///
573	/// **Why a ledger and not a pool size.** The queue runs one job at a time (#326, road map
574	/// 2's 7e) and stays that way; what can run beside its job is an Export… sheet, which a
575	/// person started and which is never held (CX-18 (6)). So the question a queued AV1 or VP9
576	/// job asks is not "how many jobs" but "does the memory the others hold, with mine, fit", and
577	/// the answer has to see the sheets too — which is why the account is one shared object
578	/// both writers book into, rather than state inside `ExportQueueController`.
579	///
580	/// **The budget is a quarter of physical memory**, G-37's share for graphic rasters, so an
581	/// export's two large consumers stay within half the Mac together. A job is admitted when
582	/// nothing is booked — one export always runs, however large — or when the booked costs and
583	/// its own fit.

585	/// Main thread only, like the queue and the sheets that book into it, and AppKit-free so a
586	/// probe compiles it headless (`tools/proof/encoder_limit_probe.swift`).
587	final class ExportEncoderLedger {
588	    /// The app's one ledger. The queue observes it and the sheets book into it.
589	    static let shared = ExportEncoderLedger()
590	
591	    /// Posted after a booking is added or removed, with the ledger as the `object`. The
592	    /// queue re-runs `start()` on it, so a held job launches when a booking ends.
593	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name(
594	        "com.kgalligan.framejob.exportEncoderLedgerDidChange")
595	
596	    /// The Mac's memory the budget is a share of — `ProcessInfo`'s, which a probe sets to
597	    /// ask what a Mac of another size would admit.
598	    var physicalMemory: UInt64
599	
600	    private var entries: [(token: UInt64, cost: UInt64)] = []
601	    private var nextToken: UInt64 = 1
602	
603	    init(physicalMemory: UInt64 = ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory) {
604	        self.physicalMemory = physicalMemory
605	    }
606	
607	    /// What bundled-encoder exports may hold together, in bytes.
608	    var budget: UInt64 { Self.budget(physicalMemory: physicalMemory) }
609	
610	    /// Each running booking's cost, in booking order.
611	    var runningCosts: [UInt64] { entries.map(\.cost) }

613	    // MARK: - The rule
614	
615	    /// A quarter of physical memory (CX-18 (3)).
616	    static func budget(physicalMemory: UInt64) -> UInt64 { physicalMemory / 4 }
617	
618	    /// Whether a job costing `cost` may start beside `running`: always when nothing runs,
619	    /// else when the sum fits `budget` (CX-18 (5)).
620	    static func admits(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> Bool {
621	        guard !running.isEmpty else { return true }
622	        let (inUse, over) = running.reduce((UInt64(0), false)) { sum, next in
623	            let added = sum.0.addingReportingOverflow(next)
624	            return (added.partialValue, sum.1 || added.overflow)
625	        }
626	        let total = inUse.addingReportingOverflow(cost)
627	        return !over && !total.overflow && total.partialValue <= budget
628	    }

631	    static func waitingSentence(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> String {
632	        let inUse = running.reduce(UInt64(0)) { $0 &+ $1 }
633	        return "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about "
634	            + "\(gigabytes(inUse)) of the \(gigabytes(budget)) this Mac allows them, and this "
635	            + "one needs about \(gigabytes(cost))."

639	        String(format: "%.1f GB", Double(bytes) / 1_073_741_824)

645	    /// running job, which a waiting job is behind anyway). True for an AVFoundation row.
646	    func admits(_ settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> Bool {
647	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return true }
648	        return Self.admits(
649	            cost: ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget),
650	            running: costs(ignoring: token), budget: budget)
651	    }
652	
653	    /// The held sentence for `settings`, or nil when it is admitted.
654	    func waitingSentence(for settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> String? {
655	        guard !admits(settings, ignoring: token) else { return nil }
656	        return Self.waitingSentence(

659	    }

661	    private func costs(ignoring token: UInt64?) -> [UInt64] {
662	        entries.filter { $0.token != token }.map(\.cost)
663	    }

670	    func begin(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> UInt64? {
671	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return nil }
672	        let token = nextToken
673	        nextToken += 1

681	    /// observer may launch its next job — and book it — inside this call, which is why a
682	    /// caller clears its own token BEFORE calling this.
683	    func end(_ token: UInt64?) {
684	        guard let token, let index = entries.firstIndex(where: { $0.token == token }) else {
685	            return
686	        }
687	        entries.remove(at: index)

689	    }

693	    }
