34	///
35	/// **The agent's `export` is a job here (spec §11 #326).** It keeps its
36	/// refusals synchronous, then enqueues exactly as Add to Queue does and
37	/// answers the job's id at once; `export_status` follows the job and
38	/// `cancel_export` calls `cancel` (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`). The
39	/// queue's own API is unchanged by it: the mirror reads `job(_:)` and
40	/// observes `didChangeNotification` like the window does, and no tool
41	/// exists for a person's own queued job.
42	///
43	/// **One job at a time, on the MAIN thread, a fresh `Exporter` for each.**
44	/// `Exporter.export`'s own doc says main-thread-only and one export at a time,
45	/// and it means both: it schedules a run-loop `Timer` — which must be
46	/// invalidated on the thread it was scheduled on — and calls its progress and
47	/// completion handlers on the main thread. So this is a CHAIN and not a pool:
48	/// `start()` runs the head of the list and each completion runs the next. A
49	/// `DispatchQueue` of exporters would be the wrong shape whatever the machine's
50	/// core count, and not only because of the timer — an `Exporter` carries
51	/// per-export state (`recipeKey`, `cancelRequested`, the loudness scratch
52	/// buffer), which is why each job gets its own rather than one being reset
53	/// between jobs. Every method below is main-thread-only for that reason, like
54	/// the exporter it drives.
55	///
56	/// **What a job holds is the whole of what it will write, captured when it was
57	/// confirmed.** The `ReelProject` is a handle and handles are immutable (spec
58	/// §5.5) — every edit and every undo makes a NEW one — so a queued write cannot
59	/// be reached by an edit made after it, and it needs no clone: `Exporter.export`
60	/// publishes it on a `RecipeSource` key it mints for itself, never the
61	/// document's, so even the frames the compositor serves this export come from
62	/// this handle. The document may be edited, undone or CLOSED while the job
63	/// waits; the handle is retained here and the Rust project behind it lives
64	/// until the job is gone.
65	///
66	/// **And the media URLs are resolved at ENQUEUE, which is what makes them part
67	/// of that same snapshot.** `ProjectDocument.mediaURLs()` resolves a bookmark
68	/// and asks the filesystem whether the file is there (`mediaURL(for:)`), so it
69	/// is a reading of the disk at the moment it is called: resolving at RUN time
70	/// would silently pick up a Relink… or a moved file from after the job was
71	/// queued, which is the exact change an immutable job exists to exclude. That
72	/// rule is structural here rather than remembered — `enqueue` takes a
73	/// `[UInt32: URL]` and a job holds no document, so there is nothing to ask
74	/// again later even if somebody wanted to.
75	///
76	/// **The REVERSE resolution is the third thing in that snapshot, and it was
77	/// missing.** Handle immutability covers the project and nothing beside it:
78	/// which clips play from a pre-rendered backwards file is a reading of the
79	/// disk too (`ProjectDocument.reverseState`, `ReverseCache.existing`), it
80	/// cannot be derived from a bare handle, and it lives in a side table keyed by
81	/// object IDENTITY — which the document overwrites on every edit and removes
82	/// when it closes. So a job queued from a timeline holding a reversed clip
83	/// used to answer `.none` the moment anything was edited, and `.none` means
84	/// "not reversed": the export took the forward asset at the mirrored source
85	/// window, unslated and unreported. It is captured here at enqueue, exactly as
86	/// the URLs are, and PINNED to this job's own handle for the length of its
87	/// write (`ReverseSource.pin`). Anything else the picture depends on that is
88	/// neither in the handle nor derivable from it joins that list.
89	///
90	/// **A bundled-encoder job also waits for memory (spec §11 CX-18).** An AV1 or VP9 job
91	/// starts only while `ExportEncoderLedger` admits it: nothing else booked, or the running
92	/// encoder exports — an Export… sheet's beside this queue's — fitting with it in a quarter
93	/// of physical memory. A held job says why in its `message` and is PASSED OVER by a later
94	/// job the ledger admits, an AVFoundation job always; the chain stays one job at a time.
95	/// The running job is booked from just before its `export` call to its finish, and a
96	/// booking's end — the queue's own or a sheet's — re-runs `start()` through the ledger's
97	/// notification.
98	final class ExportQueueController {
99	    /// The app's one queue: the export sheet's Add to Queue fills it and
100	    /// Window ▸ Export Queue shows it.
101	    static let shared = ExportQueueController()
102	
103	    /// Where a job is. A closed set with no associated values, so the two
104	    /// readers ask it different questions without either having to spell a
105	    /// message: the window's row draws its own wording (which carries a
106	    /// percentage the state cannot know), and a probe compares the case and
107	    /// reads `Job.message` for the sentence. The raw values are the same
108	    /// strings a probe writes into its JSON answer.
109	    enum State: String {
110	        /// Queued and not started. The only state a job can be enqueued in.
111	        case waiting
112	        /// The one job an `Exporter` is running. At most one at any moment.
113	        case running
114	        /// The file landed.
115	        case completed
116	        /// Stopped by a person, either before it started or mid-write — in
117	        /// which case its half-written file has been removed.
118	        case cancelled
119	        /// The exporter refused or failed. Whatever it had written is LEFT on
120	        /// disk, which is `ExportProgressSheetController`'s posture and not a
121	        /// new one: a cancel is a person saying "not this", where a failure is
122	        /// evidence, and the file names itself in the message.
123	        case failed
124	
125	        /// Whether the job is over, however it ended — the test for "may be
126	        /// removed from the list" and for "no longer holds a project handle
127	        /// worth keeping".
128	        var isFinished: Bool { self == .completed || self == .cancelled || self == .failed }
129	    }
130	
131	    /// One confirmed export. Everything it needs was read when it was
132	    /// enqueued; see the type doc for why that is the whole point of it.
133	    struct Job {
134	        /// Monotonic within one launch. The window's rows and every method
135	        /// below address a job by this rather than by index, because a job can
136	        /// be removed from the middle of the list while a later one runs.
137	        let id: UInt64
138	        /// The timeline as it was confirmed — immutable, and retained here, so
139	        /// the document behind it may be edited, undone or closed.
140	        ///
141	        /// A FINISHED job goes on holding it, and that is a real cost stated
142	        /// rather than hidden: a handle is the project's model and not its
143	        /// media, so it is JSON-sized, and Clear Finished (or Remove) is what
144	        /// releases it along with the row that says where the file went.
145	        /// Dropping the handle at the finish would buy those bytes back and
146	        /// cost the field its `let` — an immutable job whose contents change
147	        /// once is a harder thing to reason about than a list somebody tidies.
148	        let project: ReelProject
149	        /// The media files as they resolved AT ENQUEUE.
150	        let urls: [UInt32: URL]
151	        /// Which of this timeline's clips play from a pre-rendered backwards
152	        /// file, as that resolved AT ENQUEUE — the type doc's third piece of
153	        /// the snapshot. Read from `ReverseSource` here and published back to
154	        /// it under this job's own handle while the job runs, because the
155	        /// document's copy is overwritten by the next edit and dropped when it
156	        /// closes.
157	        let reverse: ReverseResolution
158	        let settings: ExportSettings
159	        let destination: URL
160	        /// What this export asks of the PICTURE besides the timeline — the
161	        /// burn-in (`RecipeOptions`). Carried per job, because two jobs from
162	        /// one document may legitimately differ in it.
163	        let options: RecipeOptions
164	        /// The document's compiled graphics as they stood AT ENQUEUE (G-13) —
165	        /// the type doc's list again: a module saved after Add to Queue is not
166	        /// in the handle, and the document's set is swapped by that save and
167	        /// dropped when it closes. `Exporter.export` pins it for the write.
168	        let graphics: GraphicSet?
169	        var state: State = .waiting
170	        /// 0…1, and only meaningful while `state` is `.running`.
171	        var progress: Double = 0
172	        /// The line a person reads when it is over: what was written and what
173	        /// the file measured, or why it stopped — plus the one thing worth
174	        /// saying mid-flight, that a cancel is in hand. While it waits, the
175	        /// ledger's sentence when the memory limit holds it (CX-18), else nil.
176	        var message: String?
177	        /// What the exporter says it is doing right now, or nil for "writing",
178	        /// which is the caller's own wording. Today the only phase is the
179	        /// loudness measurement, which on an audio-only export is half the wait
180	        /// and the half where nothing is on disk yet.
181	        ///
182	        /// A field of its own rather than a use of `message`, because the two
183	        /// are written by different things at the same time: the progress tick
184	        /// arrives ten times a second and would otherwise wipe the "Stopping…"
185	        /// a person had just asked for.
186	        var phase: String?
187	        /// Set on a COMPLETED job when a later job starts writing to the same
188	        /// path, because from that moment this row's file is not this row's
189	        /// any more — `Exporter.startWriting` removes whatever is at the
190	        /// destination before it builds its pipeline, so the earlier export is
191	        /// gone whether the later one succeeds, fails or is cancelled.
192	        ///
193	        /// The row stops claiming "Exported …" and stops offering Show in
194	        /// Finder. It is a fact about what happened rather than a state: the
195	        /// job really did complete, and rewriting its `state` would lose that.
196	        ///
197	        /// One case marks it where the file in fact survives, and it is the
198	        /// honest direction of the two: a later job whose COMPOSITION fails to
199	        /// build returns before the delete, so nothing was destroyed. It is
200	        /// left alone rather than reached for, because knowing which failures
201	        /// precede the delete means reading `Exporter`'s stages from here, and
202	        /// a shared destination implies a shared project — a build that failed
203	        /// for job 2 would almost always have failed for job 1.
204	        var superseded: Bool = false
205	        /// What the graphics warned while a COMPLETED job's file was drawn
206	        /// (G-24 (c)): the row's count and its tooltip's list.
207	        var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning] = []
208	        var cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning] = []  // spec §11 CU-37 (c)
209	        /// What a COMPLETED job's sound measured, read off its exporter at the
210	        /// finish — the figures the row's message summarises, kept whole for
211	        /// `export_status`'s `loudness` (spec §11 #326). nil otherwise.
212	        var loudness: ExportLoudness? = nil
213	
214	        /// What the row calls this job. The file name and not the path: the
215	        /// row is narrow, and the full path is the tooltip's job.
216	        var name: String { destination.lastPathComponent }
217	    }
218	
219	    /// Posted after any change to `jobs` — an enqueue, a progress tick, a
220	    /// finish, a cancel, a removal — with the controller as the `object`, so
221	    /// an observer of the shared queue is never woken by a probe's own
222	    /// instance. Main thread, like everything else here.
223	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name(
224	        "com.kgalligan.framejob.exportQueueDidChange")
225	
226	    /// Every job this launch still knows about, in the order they were added.
227	    /// A finished one stays until it is removed, because "it is done and here
228	    /// is where it went" is the queue's other job.
229	    private(set) var jobs: [Job] = []
230	
231	    /// The exporter running `runningID`'s job, and nil whenever nothing is
232	    /// running. Set and cleared together with the job's state, so `isIdle` can
233	    /// be answered from `jobs` alone.
234	    private var exporter: Exporter?
235	
236	    /// The handle whose reverse resolution is pinned in `ReverseSource` right
237	    /// now — the running job's, and nil whenever nothing is running. Held
238	    /// separately from the job so that `launch` and `finished` are provably one
239	    /// pin and one release, whatever happens to the list in between.
240	    private var pinnedProject: ReelProject?
241	
242	    /// The running job's booking in the encoder ledger (CX-18), nil whenever nothing runs
243	    /// or the running job is an AVFoundation one. Taken BEFORE `end` in `finished`: the
244	    /// ledger's post can launch — and book — the next job inside that call.
245	    private var ledgerToken: UInt64?
246	
247	    private let ledger = ExportEncoderLedger.shared
248	
249	    /// True only while `start()` is inside `Exporter.export`. An early refusal
250	    /// — `noPlan`, `emptyTimeline` — completes SYNCHRONOUSLY, so `finished`
251	    /// can run before `export` has returned; without this flag the next job
252	    /// would be launched from inside the previous one's stack frame and a
253	    /// queue of refusals would recurse as deep as it is long. With it, a
254	    /// re-entrant `start()` is refused and the frame already on the stack
255	    /// picks the next job up in its own loop.
256	    private var isLaunching = false
257	
258	    private var nextID: UInt64 = 1
259	
260	    /// Internal rather than private, and deliberately: a proof compiles a
261	    /// probe out of `app/Sources` and makes its OWN queue, so that running two
262	    /// jobs in a script cannot disturb — or be disturbed by — the app's shared
263	    /// one. It is the same reason `ExportPresetsStore` is a value a test can
264	    /// make.
265	    init() {
266	        // A booking's end — a sheet's as much as this queue's — may admit a held job.
267	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
268	            self, selector: #selector(ledgerChanged(_:)),
269	            name: ExportEncoderLedger.didChangeNotification, object: ledger)
270	    }
271	
272	    @objc private func ledgerChanged(_ note: Notification) { start() }
273	
274	    @available(*, unavailable)
275	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
276	        fatalError("ExportQueueController does not support NSCoder")
277	    }
278	
279	    // MARK: - Asking
280	
281	    /// Nothing waiting and nothing running. The queue's own "are we there
282	    /// yet", and what a probe spins the run loop until.
283	    ///
284	    /// Answered from `jobs` rather than from `exporter`, so it means the same
285	    /// thing to a caller that cannot see the private state.
286	    var isIdle: Bool {
287	        !jobs.contains { $0.state == .waiting || $0.state == .running }
288	    }
289	
290	    /// The job an exporter is writing right now, if any.
291	    var runningJob: Job? { jobs.first { $0.state == .running } }
292	
293	    /// How many are still queued behind it.
294	    var waitingCount: Int { jobs.filter { $0.state == .waiting }.count }
295	
296	    func job(_ id: UInt64) -> Job? { jobs.first { $0.id == id } }
297	
298	    // MARK: - Filling
299	
300	    /// Adds one confirmed export and starts the queue if it is not already
301	    /// running. Answers the job's id, so a caller can follow it.
302	    ///
303	    /// The arguments are `Exporter.export`'s, and that is not a coincidence:
304	    /// a job is exactly the call that will be made, held until its turn. Both
305	    /// `project` and `urls` are read by the CALLER, at the moment the save
306	    /// panel answered (`EditorViewController.enqueueExport`), which is what
307	    /// the type doc means by capturing at enqueue.
308	    ///
309	    /// **Two jobs may name one file, and the queue still does not refuse it —
310	    /// but it no longer pretends the person was warned.** The reason first
311	    /// given here was that "the save panel asked about replacing an existing
312	    /// file both times", and that is false in exactly the case that matters:
313	    /// `NSSavePanel` prompts only when something is at the path as Save is
314	    /// confirmed, and job 1 spends its build and its whole loudness
315	    /// measurement pass with nothing at the destination — `Exporter.export`
316	    /// does both before `startWriting` deletes and `AVAssetWriter` creates —
317	    /// so two Add to Queue actions in quick succession are never asked
318	    /// anything. Refusing here would still be wrong: overwriting your own
319	    /// export is a thing a person is allowed to do, and the queue must not be
320	    /// the one place in the app where they may not. What was wrong was the
321	    /// silence AFTERWARDS, and `launch` is where that is answered — the
322	    /// earlier row is marked `superseded` the moment a later job starts
323	    /// writing to its path, so no row goes on offering a file that another
324	    /// job has since deleted or replaced.
325	    @discardableResult
326	    func enqueue(
327	        project: ReelProject, urls: [UInt32: URL], settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL,
328	        options: RecipeOptions = .none, graphics: GraphicSet? = nil
329	    ) -> UInt64 {
330	        let id = nextID
331	        nextID += 1
332	        jobs.append(
333	            Job(
334	                id: id, project: project, urls: urls,
335	                // The third piece of the enqueue-time snapshot; the type doc
336	                // says why it cannot be left to be asked again at run time.
337	                reverse: ReverseSource.shared.resolution(publishedFor: project),
338	                settings: settings, destination: url, options: options, graphics: graphics))
339	        didChange()
340	        start()
341	        return id
342	    }
343	
344	    // MARK: - Running
345	
346	    /// Runs the first waiting job the encoder ledger admits, if nothing is
347	    /// running already — passing over a held one (CX-18 (7)). Idempotent
348	    /// and safe to call at any time: `enqueue` calls it, every completion
349	    /// calls it, the ledger's change calls it, and a caller may call it itself.
350	    ///
351	    /// The loop is for the synchronous-refusal case `isLaunching` describes: a
352	    /// job the exporter refuses without ever going asynchronous has already
353	    /// finished by the time `launch` returns, and this frame takes the next
354	    /// one rather than recursing into it.
355	    func start() {
356	        guard !isLaunching else { return }
357	        isLaunching = true
358	        defer { isLaunching = false }
359	        while exporter == nil, let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: {
360	            $0.state == .waiting && ledger.admits($0.settings)
361	        }) {
362	            launch(at: index)
363	        }
364	        noteHeld()
365	    }
366	
367	    /// Every waiting encoder job's `message` set to why it is held, or cleared when it is
368	    /// not — leaving out this queue's own running booking, which it waits behind anyway.
369	    private func noteHeld() {
370	        var changed = false
371	        for index in jobs.indices
372	        where jobs[index].state == .waiting && jobs[index].settings.writer != nil {
373	            let sentence = ledger.waitingSentence(for: jobs[index].settings, ignoring: ledgerToken)
374	            if jobs[index].message != sentence {
375	                jobs[index].message = sentence
376	                changed = true
377	            }
378	        }
379	        if changed { didChange() }
380	    }
381	
382	    /// One job handed to one fresh `Exporter`. The exporter is stored BEFORE
383	    /// the call, because an early refusal calls back before `export` returns
384	    /// and `finished` has to find it there.
385	    private func launch(at index: Int) {
386	        let job = jobs[index]
387	        jobs[index].state = .running
388	        jobs[index].progress = 0
389	        jobs[index].message = nil
390	        jobs[index].phase = nil
391	        // Any COMPLETED row naming this same path stops claiming its file
392	        // here, and here rather than when the file is actually deleted: the
393	        // delete happens inside `Exporter.startWriting`, seconds later and in
394	        // a file this one may not reach into, and being early is the honest
395	        // direction — a row that stops offering a file just before it is
396	        // destroyed costs a person nothing, where one that offers it just
397	        // after sends them to the Finder for something that is gone.
398	        for other in jobs.indices
399	        where other != index && jobs[other].state == .completed
400	            && jobs[other].destination == job.destination
401	        {
402	            jobs[other].superseded = true
403	        }
404	        // The job's own reverse resolution, held against its own handle for
405	        // exactly the length of this write. At most one pin exists at a time,
406	        // which is the invariant `ReverseSource.pin` asks its callers for and
407	        // which this class keeps for free by running one job at a time.
408	        ReverseSource.shared.pin(job.reverse, for: job.project)
409	        pinnedProject = job.project
410	        // Booked BEFORE `export`, whose early refusals finish synchronously inside it.
411	        ledgerToken = ledger.begin(job.settings)
412	        let exporter = Exporter()
413	        self.exporter = exporter
414	        didChange()
415	        exporter.export(
416	            project: job.project, urls: job.urls, settings: job.settings, to: job.destination,
417	            options: job.options, graphics: job.graphics,
418	            progress: { [weak self] value in self?.progressed(job.id, value) },
419	            completion: { [weak self] result in self?.finished(job.id, result) })
420	    }
421	
422	    private func progressed(_ id: UInt64, _ value: Double) {
423	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }),
424	            jobs[index].state == .running
425	        else { return }
426	        jobs[index].progress = min(max(value, 0), 1)
427	        // The exporter names its own phase while it has one. The progress
428	        // sheet asks the same question with the same call; a row that said
429	        // "Writing" through the measurement would be claiming a file that does
430	        // not exist yet.
431	        jobs[index].phase = exporter?.phaseDescription
432	        didChange()
433	    }
434	
435	    /// The one exit for all three outcomes, and the mirror of
436	    /// `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` — deliberately, because there
437	    /// must not be two accounts of what finishing an export means. The
438	    /// exporter is cleared first, so the `start()` at the foot can hand the
439	    /// next job a fresh one.
440	    private func finished(_ id: UInt64, _ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
441	        // Read BEFORE the exporter is dropped: `Exporter.finish` publishes the
442	        // measurement and then calls this, so the report is there now and only
443	        // now.
444	        let report = exporter?.loudnessReport
445	        let measured = report.map { " \($0.summary)." } ?? ""
446	        let warnings = exporter?.graphicWarnings ?? []
447	        let cursorWarnings = exporter?.cursorWarnings ?? []
448	        exporter = nil
449	        // The pin goes with the exporter, and from `pinnedProject` rather than
450	        // from the job, so that releasing it cannot depend on the job still
451	        // being in the list. Exactly one release per `launch`, which is what
452	        // `ReverseSource.pin` asks for; a pin left behind would retain the
453	        // Rust project for the life of the process.
454	        if let pinned = pinnedProject {
455	            ReverseSource.shared.unpin(pinned)
456	            pinnedProject = nil
457	        }
458	        if let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) {
459	            jobs[index].phase = nil
460	            switch result {
461	            case .success(let url):
462	                jobs[index].state = .completed
463	                jobs[index].progress = 1
464	                jobs[index].graphicWarnings = warnings
465	                jobs[index].cursorWarnings = cursorWarnings
466	                jobs[index].loudness = report
467	                // The count BEFORE the loudness figures: the row truncates
468	                // its tail (`ExportQueueRowView`).
469	                jobs[index].message = "Exported “\(url.lastPathComponent)”\(ExportStemsPipeline.summary(jobs[index].settings))."
470	                    + Exporter.graphicWarningSuffix(warnings, hover: false)
471	                    + Exporter.cursorWarningSuffix(cursorWarnings, hover: false) + measured
472	            case .failure(let error):
473	                if case Exporter.ExportError.cancelled = error {
474	                    // A cancelled job leaves nothing behind, and this line is
475	                    // DEFENCE IN DEPTH rather than the thing that achieves it
476	                    // — measured, because the obvious reading is wrong and a
477	                    // reader who believes it would be relying on a guarantee
478	                    // this line does not provide. Both pipelines already
479	                    // clean up after themselves: `AVAssetWriter.cancelWriting()`
480	                    // removes its own part-file (`ExporterWriter.swift` says
481	                    // so where it calls it) and `ImageSequenceWriter.report`
482	                    // removes its own. Deleting this line changes no observable
483	                    // outcome — phase 7's proof mutated it away and scored
484	                    // 77/77 — so the check beside it is written as the OUTCOME
485	                    // ("nothing is left behind") and not as a guard on this
486	                    // call. Keep it: it costs nothing, it states the policy
487	                    // where the policy is decided, and it is what holds if a
488	                    // third pipeline ever arrives that is less tidy.
489	                    // `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` is the same line
490	                    // for the same reason.
491	                    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: jobs[index].destination)
492	                    jobs[index].state = .cancelled
493	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
494	                    jobs[index].message = "Cancelled."
495	                } else {
496	                    jobs[index].state = .failed
497	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
498	                    jobs[index].message = error.localizedDescription
499	                }
500	            }
501	        }
502	        didChange()
503	        // Cleared before `end`, whose post may launch and book the next job.
504	        let token = ledgerToken
505	        ledgerToken = nil
506	        ledger.end(token)
507	        start()
508	    }
509	
510	    // MARK: - Stopping and tidying
511	
512	    /// Stops one job, whether it has started or not.
513	    ///
514	    /// A WAITING job is simply marked: it has no exporter to stop and no file
515	    /// to remove, because nothing has been written under its name. A RUNNING
516	    /// one is asked to stop and answers through `finished`, which is where its
517	    /// file is removed — one exit, so a cancel from the window and a cancel
518	    /// from a script clean up identically. A finished job is left alone.
519	    func cancel(_ id: UInt64) {
520	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return }
521	        switch jobs[index].state {
522	        case .waiting:
523	            jobs[index].state = .cancelled

`encoder_speed` (`faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`) is `av1`'s and `av1_webm`'s
alone and is refused on every other preset, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm` (one speed)
included; the done answer names it. On those two and `vp9_webm`, `video_bitrate` is a soft
cap: the file usually comes in well under it, and very detailed footage can go
up to about 1.25 times over it on AV1 and about 1.15 times on VP9. On `vp9_alpha_webm` it
is the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone, and the alpha stream comes on top of it
(about 6–15 % of the video at 1080p, up to about 39 % at 640 × 360, measured). `vp9_alpha_webm`
keeps a transparent canvas, as `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` and `apng` do, and refuses a
`[width, height]` of another shape. What each option means is in [Export](export.md).
